title: Legislative Proposal to Implement the Regulatory Regime for Stablecoin Issuers in Hong Kong – Consultation Conclusions
supersedes_or_amends: Legislative Proposal to Implement the Regulatory Regime for Stablecoin Issuers in Hong Kong – Consultation Paper
summary: Published jointly by the FSTB and HKMA in July 2024, this paper responds to 108 submissions on the December 2023 consultation paper. It confirms the authorities will go ahead with a licensing regime for fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) issuers. It keeps the core proposals: full reserve backing, redemption rights, and HKMA licensing. It clarifies what counts as 'actively marketing' to the Hong Kong public, and confirms HKD-referenced coins issued from outside Hong Kong are still covered. A bill was to go to the Legislative Council (LegCo) later in 2024.

key_points.point: The scope was narrowed so the regime targets stablecoins run on distributed ledgers not controlled by a single party, rather than covering privately-run ledgers too.
Both single-currency and multi-currency referenced stablecoins stay in scope. Multi-currency issuers face rules scaled to the extra complexity of managing reserves in several currencies.
Whether marketing counts as 'active marketing' depends on factors like the language used, whether the audience is Hong Kong-based, and use of a Hong Kong domain name.
An overseas entity issuing a Hong Kong dollar-referenced stablecoin still needs an HKMA licence, even if it operates outside Hong Kong, because of the currency's local importance.
Agents or intermediaries who market a licensed issuer's stablecoin on its behalf do not themselves need a licence, but anyone promoting an unlicensed issuer's coin commits an offence.
The authorities confirmed a bill to bring in the regime would go to the Legislative Council later in 2024, with the HKMA to issue licensing and supervisory guidelines afterwards.
The six-month grace period for existing issuers to apply for a licence was kept, informed partly by experience running the HKMA's stablecoin issuer sandbox.

numbers_and_dates.item: Grace period retained for pre-existing issuers

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this shows how the government tightened the stablecoin regime after feedback, including confirming HKD-pegged coins are covered even from outside Hong Kong. This matters for cross-border product screening and checking a stablecoin counterparty's licensing status.
reading_guide: Read the Introduction (pages 3-4) and the responses under Scope and Coverage (section 1, pages 4-7) and Way Forward (section 12, page 29). You should read it alongside the original consultation paper, which it amends rather than replaces.
flags: This is the second half of a two-part package — read together with the December 2023 consultation paper (id 167649d1bc28), which it amends rather than replaces.
The regime described here was still pre-bill at the time of writing; the enacted Stablecoins Ordinance and HKMA guidelines are the current binding text and should be checked for further changes.

obligations: If the bank or an affiliate issues or plans to issue an HKD-referenced stablecoin from any location, treat HKMA licensing as required regardless of where the issuing entity is based, per para 3.1.5, p.9.
controls_and_monitoring: If the bank acts as an agent/intermediary marketing a stablecoin, confirm the underlying issuer is licensed before promoting it, since marketing an unlicensed issuer's coin is itself an offence (para 3.1.4, p.9).
counterparty_due_diligence: When assessing a stablecoin issuer counterparty, check whether its ledger is genuinely decentralised (no single controlling party) since that affects whether it falls under the regime at all (para 1.4, p.5).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Flag to the board that the stablecoin licensing bill was expected in the Legislative Council later in 2024, so any stablecoin-related product roadmap needs a checkpoint once the ordinance and HKMA guidelines are finalised.

title: Legislative Proposal to Implement the Regulatory Regime for Stablecoin Issuers in Hong Kong – Consultation Conclusions
supersedes_or_amends: Consultation paper on legislative proposal to implement the regulatory regime for stablecoin issuers in Hong Kong (27 December 2023)
summary: This paper sets out the FSTB's and HKMA's final positions on the future fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) issuer licensing regime, after a two-month consultation that drew 108 responses. It confirms the regime covers stablecoins on decentralised distributed ledgers referencing one or more fiat currencies, and requires full reserve backing at all times. High-quality liquid assets must be kept separate from the issuer's own assets. It bans paying interest to holders, requires local incorporation and Hong Kong-based key management, and sets minimum capital at the higher of HK$25 million or 1% of stablecoins in circulation. It also confirms redemption must happen within one business day, and that only specified licensed entities may offer FRS to the public. A bill was to go to the Legislative Council (LegCo) later in 2024.

key_points.point: The definition of a regulated stablecoin was narrowed to those run on a 'decentralised distributed ledger', meaning no single party can unilaterally control or materially change how it works.
Both single-currency and multi-currency fiat-referenced stablecoins (FRS) stay in scope, because both can pose financial stability risk through their links to the traditional financial system.
Stablecoins in circulation must be backed 1:1 by reserve assets at all times; issuers must show steps such as over-collateralisation to keep meeting this on an ongoing basis.

Reserve assets must be high quality and highly liquid. Allowed categories include cash and banknotes, deposits at licensed banks, high-credit-quality government or central-bank securities, related overnight reverse repos, and tokenised versions of these assets.

Reserve assets must generally be in the same currency the stablecoin references; a currency mismatch needs the Monetary Authority's (MA's) prior approval and may trigger extra rules such as over-collateralisation. HKD-referenced stablecoins may explicitly hold USD-denominated reserves.

Reserve assets must be kept separate from the issuer's own assets and safeguarded under an effective trust arrangement. Safekeeping with licensed Hong Kong banks is favoured, though offshore placement may be allowed case by case.
Issuers must get monthly independent auditor attestation of reserve assets, though how often this is disclosed publicly may be reduced from the original proposal after industry feedback.
Issuers may not pay interest to stablecoin holders, though non-interest marketing incentives stay allowed.

Redemption requests must be met within one business day in normal conditions, at par value, without undue cost or unreasonable conditions; issuers expecting difficulty must seek the MA's prior approval.
Issuers may only carry out activities that support stablecoin issuance, such as wallet services for their own coin; lending and financial intermediation are explicitly excluded.
Non-Hong Kong incorporated applicants, other than authorized institutions, must set up a Hong Kong subsidiary, and key executives, the chief executive and alternate, must be based in Hong Kong.
Minimum paid-up share capital is set at whichever is greater of HK$25 million or 1% of the stablecoins in circulation, valued at par, down from the 2% originally proposed.

Issuers must publish a white paper, ready at the licence-application stage, disclosing risks, technology, issuance and redemption mechanics, holder rights and fees, and must notify the MA before publishing it.
Issuers must run an annual risk assessment of internal controls, risk management and governance, and keep incident-management policies covering monitoring, response and reporting to the MA.
A separate AML guideline will be issued for stablecoin issuers, matching FATF standards, including transaction monitoring and travel-rule compliance.

Only specified licensed entities, licensed FRS issuers, authorized institutions, and licensed corporations or virtual asset trading platforms authorised to deal in FRS, may offer FRS to the public. These entities need no separate MA licence to offer FRS but must meet their own regime's rules.

Any FRS issuance actively marketed to the Hong Kong public, even by an entity based outside Hong Kong, falls within the MA's licensing reach. Offering a licensed issuer's coin as agent or intermediary does not itself need a licence, but promoting an unlicensed issuer's coin is an offence for everyone involved.
A six-month grace period was set for existing stablecoin issuers to come into compliance or wind down after the regime starts.
The authorities planned to introduce the enabling bill to the Legislative Council later in 2024, with licensing and supervisory guidelines to follow.

numbers_and_dates.value: greater of HK$25 million or 1% of FRS in circulation

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is the direct policy blueprint for what became Hong Kong's stablecoin issuer licensing regime. A bank issuing a stablecoin, partnering with an issuer, offering FRS to clients, or acting as reserve custodian needs every reserve, redemption, capital and offering rule here reflected in its own controls.

quote.text: the amount of FRS issued must always be fully backed by reserve assets

reading_guide: Read the full body, from Introduction through Way Forward (paragraphs 1-12); the Annex list of respondents (pages 30 onward) can be skipped.
flags: This consultation conclusions paper was later implemented and superseded by the enacted Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) and its subsidiary guidelines — verify final rule text against the enacted law rather than relying solely on this document for current obligations.

obligations: If the bank itself applies for an FRS issuer licence, ensure full reserve backing at all times with high-quality, highly liquid, currency-matched assets (para 3.2.3, 3.2.9-3.2.10).

If offering FRS to clients as an authorized institution (a 'specified licensed entity'), comply with the bank's own applicable regulatory requirements and seek necessary approvals before offering (para 4.3).
Do not promote or facilitate the marketing of unlicensed FRS issuance to Hong Kong clients — this is an offence for any party involved, including agents/intermediaries (para 3.1.4).
controls_and_monitoring: Reserve segregation, trust arrangement, and monthly independent-auditor attestation controls if the bank or a group entity issues or custodies FRS reserves (para 3.2.11-3.2.20).
Annual risk assessment and incident-management/reporting processes for any FRS-related business (para 3.2.41-3.2.42).
notifications_reporting: Notify the MA before publishing an FRS white paper, and seek MA prior approval for any anticipated redemption delay beyond one business day (para 3.2.25, 3.2.35).
Seek MA prior approval for currency mismatch between an FRS's reference currency and its reserve assets (para 3.2.10).
counterparty_due_diligence: Verify an FRS issuer counterparty maintains full reserve backing, an effective trust/segregation arrangement, and monthly independent attestations before relying on or distributing its stablecoin (para 3.2.3, 3.2.11-3.2.20).
Check that an FRS issuer counterparty does not pay interest to holders and does not conduct lending/financial intermediation activities beyond permitted ancillary activities (para 3.2.23, 3.2.28).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: The board/risk committee should be briefed on the full scope of reserve, capital, redemption, offering and AML requirements this paper sets out, since they define both the bar for the bank's own potential stablecoin activity and the due-diligence bar for any FRS issuer counterparty.

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Darryl Chan on Stablecoin Issuer Sandbox
summary: The HKMA announced three participants had now been admitted to its stablecoin issuer sandbox, testing use cases in payments, supply-chain management and capital markets. It set out what admission needs, a demonstrable, compliant business plan, and repeated that joining the sandbox is not a substitute for a future licence. The same day, the FSTB and HKMA jointly issued their conclusions on the stablecoin issuer legislative proposal. They said they would aim to introduce the bill to the Legislative Council (LegCo) by year end. It also repeats public warnings about scams misusing the sandbox's name.

key_points.point: The HKMA admitted its first batch of three sandbox participants, whose proposed stablecoin use cases cover payments, supply-chain management, and capital-markets applications.

Sandbox testing will focus particularly on operational and technology risk, including reserve asset quality and liquidity, timely redemption, wallet and private-key management, and anti-money-laundering controls.
Sandbox participants must not raise money from the public or offer investment products in the sandbox's name, and cannot use public funds at the initial testing stage.
The conclusions on the stablecoin issuer legislative proposal were published the same day; the authorities said they would aim to introduce the bill to the Legislative Council by the end of 2024.

numbers_and_dates.item: Target for introducing the stablecoin bill to LegCo

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this confirms the sandbox moved from concept to live participants. It gives the legislative timetable compliance should track, for when a formal stablecoin issuer licensing regime, and any bank due-diligence duties toward licensees, would start.
reading_guide: Read in full; each paragraph is short. The companion conclusions paper has the substantive rulebook detail.

controls_and_monitoring: If assessing a stablecoin sandbox participant as a partner or client, review its published use case and the risk areas the HKMA said it would test (reserve quality/liquidity, redemption timeliness, key management, AML controls).
counterparty_due_diligence: Confirm sandbox admission against the HKMA's published participant list; sandbox status does not equal a licence or HKMA endorsement.
Watch for entities falsely marketing stablecoins or products using sandbox branding; report suspected misuse.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Note the legislative timetable (bill targeted by end-2024) so the board can anticipate when formal stablecoin issuer licensing obligations and bank due-diligence duties will arise.

title: HKMA announces stablecoin issuer sandbox participants
summary: The HKMA announced the first participants admitted to the stablecoin issuer sandbox launched in March 2024. They are RD InnoTech Limited; JINGDONG Coinlink Technology Hong Kong Limited; and a joint group of Animoca Brands Limited, Hong Kong Telecommunications (HKT) Limited, and Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) Limited. Participants were picked for showing genuine interest, a reasonable business plan, and a proposed operation of manageable, limited scope. At this initial stage, sandbox participants will not handle public funds or seek public funding, and the public was warned to watch for related scams.

key_points.point: Three sandbox participant groups were admitted: RD InnoTech Limited; JINGDONG Coinlink Technology Hong Kong Limited; and a joint group with Animoca Brands, HKT, and Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong).
At this initial stage, sandbox participants will not handle the general public's money or seek public funding, and will not offer any products tied to the sandbox.
The HKMA will make a separate announcement if participants are later allowed to handle public funds within a limited scope.
The public was warned to stay alert for possible scams claiming ties to the sandbox.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this names Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) as a stablecoin issuer sandbox participant. Where the bank is that participant, it is directly bound by the sandbox's scope limits; for other banks it signals a real, named testbed for the eventual licensing regime.

quote.text: will not handle the general public’s funds at the initial stage

reading_guide: Short; read in full.
flags: Sandbox participation explicitly excludes handling public funds initially — a common misconception to correct if assuming sandbox participants are already operational stablecoin issuers.

obligations: As a named sandbox participant (Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) Limited), follow sandbox rules, including not handling general public funds or seeking public funding at this initial stage.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: For a bank taking part in the sandbox, the board should track compliance with the sandbox's scope limits (no handling of public funds) until the HKMA announces any expansion of the testing scope.

title: Cryptoasset disclosure requirements and standard amendments
summary: A short HKMA circular tells banks that the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) published, on 17 July 2024, a final disclosure framework for banks' cryptoasset exposures. It also published a package of narrow changes to its cryptoasset capital standard, mainly refining stablecoin eligibility criteria. The HKMA states it will align its own proposed local rules from CP 24.01 with these BCBS updates, and will consult again on any major changes.

key_points.point: The BCBS's final disclosure framework requires banks to disclose standardised qualitative information on their cryptoasset activities, plus standardised quantitative data on capital, liquidity and accounting classification for those exposures.
The BCBS's targeted changes to its cryptoasset standard mainly refine which stablecoins qualify for preferential regulatory treatment, plus other technical clarifications.
The HKMA intends to align its proposed local capital framework, from CP 24.01, with these BCBS updates. It will run a fresh industry consultation on any further significant changes to local rules.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this signals CP 24.01's capital proposal is a moving target that will be refreshed to match the BCBS's finalised disclosure templates and stablecoin criteria. Compliance should not finalise cryptoasset disclosure or reporting builds against the original February 2024 text alone.

quote.text: further specify the criteria for stablecoins

reading_guide: One page; read in full.

controls_and_monitoring: Track BCBS/HKMA updates to stablecoin eligibility criteria before finalising internal Group 1b classification methodology
notifications_reporting: Anticipate a future further industry consultation from the HKMA on any major local changes flowing from the BCBS updates
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Flag to the board/risk committee that the cryptoasset capital and disclosure rulebook (CP 24.01) is being actively revised to track BCBS changes and is not yet final.

title: Cryptoasset disclosure requirements and standard amendments
summary: This is a catalogue page for a short HKMA circular. It flags two new BCBS publications, a cryptoasset disclosure framework and standard amendments, and confirms the HKMA will align CP 24.01 with them. The full circular text is attached and summarised separately.

key_points.point: The catalogue entry confirms this circular is current.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is an index only; see the attached circular text for the substance.
reading_guide: Go to the attached PDF (id 61e71f66d06e).

title: SFC warns public against unlicensed virtual asset trading platform CoinUnited.io
summary: The SFC warns that CoinUnited.io has never been licensed by, or applied to, the SFC. It offers trading in crypto, stocks, indices, forex and commodities, and had claimed a Hong Kong retail store and local hiring.

key_points.point: CoinUnited.io offers trading across crypto, stocks, indices, forex and commodities.
It previously claimed a Hong Kong flagship store and local hiring but has never been licensed by, or applied to, the SFC.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is a routine warning that illustrates a multi-asset unlicensed platform falsely implying a local physical presence.
reading_guide: Short; read in full.

title: SFC warns public of Proxinex for suspected virtual asset-related fraud
summary: SFC warns of Proxinex, where investors were told their accounts 'did not exist' when they tried to withdraw funds. The SFC suspects Proxinex used an agent operating through dating apps who fabricated documents claiming to come from a local financial regulator and institution to appear credible.

key_points.point: Investors were told their accounts 'did not exist' when trying to withdraw.
An agent is suspected of using dating apps and fabricated documents purportedly from a Hong Kong financial regulator and institution to lure investors.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is a routine warning showing a 'pig-butchering' pattern that mixes dating apps with forged documents impersonating a financial regulator.
reading_guide: Short; read in full.

title: SFC warns public of “ICE Global Professional Station” for impersonation and suspected virtual asset-related fraud
summary: SFC warns of a mobile-app product 'ICE Global Professional Station', accessed via a specific link, that copies the name and logo of the real Intercontinental Exchange to appear legitimate. A reported victim had difficulty withdrawing funds after investing in crypto products through it.

key_points.point: ICE Global Professional Station copies the name and logo of the genuine Intercontinental Exchange, which is unrelated to it.
A victim reported being unable to withdraw funds after making crypto investment deposits.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is a routine warning about brand impersonation carried out through a mobile app rather than a full website.
reading_guide: Short; read in full.

title: SFC welcomes launch of Project Ensemble Sandbox as key step in Hong Kong’s tokenisation development
summary: The SFC welcomed the HKMA's launch of the Project Ensemble Sandbox and confirmed it will jointly lead, with the HKMA, tokenisation initiatives for the asset management industry. Participating institutions will trial interbank settlement of tokenised asset deals using tokenised money, and test on-chain issuance, secondary trading, custody, and pledging across the whole product life cycle. The SFC will provide regulatory guidance and address industry concerns that come up from using the Sandbox.

key_points.point: The SFC will co-lead tokenisation work for the asset-management industry with the HKMA, to help build and grow Hong Kong's tokenisation market.
Sandbox participants will trial bank-to-bank settlement of tokenised asset deals using tokenised money, and look for hurdles across on-chain issuance, secondary trading, custody, and pledging.
The SFC and HKMA will coordinate to give regulatory guidance and resolve industry concerns raised by Sandbox trials; firms can bring the two regulators new tokenisation ideas to trial.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this confirms the SFC's shared leadership role in the Ensemble Sandbox for asset-management tokenisation. It matters if the bank's fund business wants to take part, but it creates no obligation.

quote.text: innovation and regulation can go hand in hand

reading_guide: Short; read in full.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No action is needed unless the bank's asset-management arm wants to apply to join the Sandbox. Note the SFC's joint leadership as the contact point for new tokenisation ideas.

title: HKMA launches Project Ensemble Sandbox to accelerate adoption of tokenisation (with photos)
summary: The HKMA switched on its Project Ensemble test environment, plugging in banks' own tokenised-deposit systems so they can trial settling transactions against each other and against digital assets in real time. The pilot's opening round is split into four subject areas: bonds and funds, treasury and repo activity, green finance items like carbon credits, and trade/supply-chain finance. The SFC will jointly steer the asset-management strand with the HKMA. A named list of participants sits in the attached annex.

key_points.point: Banks that connect their tokenised-deposit systems to the Sandbox can trial settling both bank-to-bank payments and asset deliveries against payment in experimental digital money.
The first round of testing is grouped into four subject areas: bonds and investment funds; treasury/repo liquidity work; green finance items such as carbon credits; and trade or supply-chain finance.
The SFC will co-lead with the HKMA on tokenisation initiatives specifically for the asset management industry.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this confirms a sandbox for tokenised deposits and asset settlement now exists. If the bank is a participant (see the annex for the list), compliance should govern sandbox activity the same way as any other pilot product, with the usual risk sign-off.

quote.text: blaze a new path for our financial markets

reading_guide: Read the press release, then check the attached Annex (d08abb207e83) only if identifying which banks/entities are named sandbox participants matters to your due diligence.

controls_and_monitoring: If participating, apply the same product-approval and risk governance to sandbox tokenised deposit activity as to any new product trial
counterparty_due_diligence: Use the participant annex to confirm whether a counterparty bank or fintech is a named Project Ensemble Sandbox participant
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Inform the board which named participants (from the annex) are direct competitors or partners in tokenised deposit experimentation, to inform the bank's own participation decision.

title: HKMA launches Project Ensemble Sandbox to accelerate adoption of tokenisation
summary: The HKMA formally launched the Project Ensemble Sandbox. It connects tokenised deposit platforms run by banks in its Architecture Community, so they can test two settlement modes between banks: payment-versus-payment and delivery-versus-payment. The pilot's first round groups test cases under four headings. These are bonds and funds; liquidity tools such as repos and treasury work; green finance such as carbon credits and EV charging; and trade and supply-chain finance. Named participants include Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng Bank, HSBC, Standard Chartered, HashKey Group, BlackRock and Ant entities, per the attached annex.

key_points.point: Banks in the Project Ensemble Architecture Community connected their own tokenised deposit systems to the sandbox. This let them test two settlement modes between banks: payment-versus-payment and delivery-versus-payment.

The pilot's first round groups test cases under four headings. These are bonds and investment funds; liquidity tools such as repos and treasury work; green finance such as carbon credits and EV charging; and trade or supply-chain finance.

Named community members taking part include Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng Bank, HSBC, Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong), HashKey Group, Ant Digital Technologies and Microsoft Hong Kong. Other participants outside the core community include BlackRock, HKEX and Cyberport.
The SFC will co-lead tokenisation work for the asset-management sector together with the HKMA.
The HKMA plans to explore working with the Hong Kong Centre of the BIS Innovation Hub and the CBDC Expert Group to push the sandbox forward.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, no duty attaches here. A compliance head at a bank in the Architecture Community should still track which use cases and controls the sandbox tests, since the list can change.
reading_guide: Read main release plus the Annex table (2 pages) listing themes, use cases and named participants.
flags: Annex explicitly states the listed themes/use cases/participants are 'subject to change'.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Tell the board about the sandbox's four test themes -- bonds/funds, liquidity, green finance, trade finance -- and that the list of themes and participants may still change (Annex, p.1-2).

title: New speech by Julia Leung: Opening remarks at Project Ensemble Sandbox Launch Ceremony
summary: A brief SFC news notice stating that a speech by Julia Leung, given at the Project Ensemble Sandbox launch ceremony, went up on the SFC website. This notice carries no substantive content of its own -- it just points readers to the separately published speech.

key_points.point: The SFC put up, on its website, a speech Julia Leung gave at the Project Ensemble Sandbox launch ceremony.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is just a pointer; no regulatory substance is captured here, since the speech text itself is not included.
reading_guide: Four-line stub; nothing further to read here.

title: List of Ensemble Architecture Community Members
summary: This is a one-page roster of the Project Ensemble Architecture Community. It lists the regulators, banks, technology firms and other bodies that helped design the Ensemble Sandbox's architecture and standards.

key_points.point: Community members include the HKMA and SFC as regulators, and the BIS Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre. Five banks take part: Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng, JPMorgan Chase, Standard Chartered (Hong Kong), and HSBC. Technology firms include Ant International, Ant Digital Technologies, Microsoft Hong Kong, R3 and WeBank Technology Services.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this identifies which banks and technology vendors are already involved in shaping the HKMA's tokenised-asset infrastructure, useful for benchmarking or partnership decisions.
reading_guide: One-page table; read in full.

counterparty_due_diligence: Cross-check whether a prospective tokenisation technology partner (e.g. R3, Ant Digital Technologies, Microsoft) is already an established Ensemble Architecture Community participant.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No escalation needed; reference list only.

title: Annex: Four main themes and their corresponding use case categories to be tested on the Project Ensemble Sandbox
summary: This annex lists eight use-case categories under the Sandbox's four themes. These are bonds and funds; repo and treasury management; carbon credits and EV charging; and supply-chain and trade finance. It names each participating Community member and non-Community organisation testing them. Named bank participants include Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng Bank, HSBC and Standard Chartered Hong Kong. Non-bank participants include HashKey Group, Ant Digital Technologies, BlackRock and several fintech and incubator firms.

key_points.point: The fixed income and investment funds theme covers bond and fund use cases. Community member participants include Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng Bank, HashKey Group, HSBC and Standard Chartered Hong Kong.
The liquidity management theme covers repo and treasury management use cases, with Bank of China (Hong Kong) and HSBC as Community members and Ant International as a non-Community participant.

The trade and supply chain finance theme covers supply-chain finance and trade finance and payments. Participants include Ant Digital Technologies, Hang Seng Bank, HSBC, Microsoft Hong Kong and Standard Chartered Hong Kong.
key_points.locator: table, Trade and supply chain finance row, p.2

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is the clearest source for which banks and fintechs are directly testing tokenised deposits and asset settlement in Hong Kong right now. It is useful for benchmarking the bank's own digital-asset strategy and spotting counterparties already engaged with the HKMA.
reading_guide: Scan the table for named participants relevant to the bank's own peer set or counterparties; the use-case category labels are self-explanatory.
flags: Participant list is stated to be updated from time to time, so treat this as a snapshot as of August 2024.

counterparty_due_diligence: Cross-reference this participant list when assessing a counterparty's digital-asset/tokenisation experience or claims of HKMA sandbox involvement
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No escalation needed; reference data only.

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Opening Remarks at Launch Ceremony for Project Ensemble Sandbox
summary: These are launch remarks for the Ensemble Sandbox, a new financial market infrastructure. It tests the full lifecycle of a tokenised-asset transaction. This covers creating and trading tokenised assets, settling payments with tokenised commercial-bank deposits, and finally settling between banks in HKMA-issued central bank digital currency (CBDC). The sandbox followed the March 2024 launch of Project Ensemble and an industry Architecture Community that co-developed its design. Early pilots cover fixed income and funds, liquidity management, green finance, and trade and supply-chain finance. The sandbox has also been cross-border linked with a Banque de France system for atomic settlement trials.

key_points.point: The Ensemble Sandbox covers the full tokenised-asset transaction lifecycle: creation/trading of tokenised assets, settling payments with tokenised commercial-bank deposits, and final interbank settlement using HKMA-issued CBDC.
Banks in the Architecture Community had by this point integrated their tokenised-deposit infrastructure with the Sandbox, enabling payment-versus-payment and delivery-versus-payment experiments.
The Sandbox's cross-border payment functionality had been successfully linked and tested with Banque de France's equivalent system for atomic cross-border settlement.
The SFC was reviewing the legal and regulatory framework for asset tokenisation to support Project Ensemble's use cases.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this confirms the Ensemble Sandbox's design links tokenised deposits directly to HKMA central bank digital currency (CBDC) settlement. A bank's tokenised-deposit product design will need to work with this HKMA-run infrastructure, not a purely private ledger.
reading_guide: Read the 'Project Ensemble' and 'Tokenising Today' sections (paras 11-49) for substance; the closing rhetorical sections on the 'four Ts' theme can be skimmed.

controls_and_monitoring: If the bank participates in Ensemble Sandbox pilots, ensure tokenised-deposit infrastructure integration and PvP/DvP experiment controls align with the shared Architecture Community standards.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Inform the board that core settlement infrastructure for tokenised deposits is being built as shared HKMA infrastructure (the Ensemble Sandbox), which will shape any future in-house tokenised-deposit product.

title: Appointments to Task Force on Promoting Web3 Development
summary: The Hong Kong government appointed three new non-official members to the Task Force on Promoting Web3 Development. The Financial Secretary chairs this Task Force, which was set up in 2023 after the 2023-24 Budget announcement. It advises on sustainable, responsible Web3 development. Official members include the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the Insurance Authority.

key_points.point: Three new non-official members, whose terms run to 30 June 2025, joined the Task Force's 18 non-official members and regulator officials.
Official members include the Chief Executives of the HKMA, SFC, Insurance Authority and HKEX, alongside senior government officials.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this has no direct compliance content. It is useful only to see which regulators and industry figures shape Hong Kong's Web3 policy direction.
reading_guide: Skim; an appointments announcement with a membership list, no substantive policy content.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No escalation needed.

title: Regulatory Regime for Stablecoin Issuers in Hong Kong
summary: This is a feature article from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) Quarterly Bulletin, published just after its July 2024 consultation conclusions. It explains in plain language why Hong Kong is regulating stablecoin issuers, covering market history such as the DeFi Summer, the TerraUSD depeg and the FTX collapse. It also covers the proposed licensing requirements and the HKMA's stablecoin issuer sandbox, which launched in July 2024. The first sandbox participants tested payments, supply chain and capital markets uses. Joining the sandbox was not required before applying for a licence. It also warns of scams that falsely claim sandbox or licensed status, and records the HKMA's plan to bring a stablecoin bill to the Legislative Council.

key_points.point: The article groups requirements into four areas: stablecoin stability, reserve safekeeping, issuer governance, and risk management including anti-money laundering controls.
Only stablecoins issued by licensed issuers were intended to be offerable to retail investors, restricting unlicensed issuers to non-retail distribution.
The sandbox, launched July 2024, lets firms test business models and get HKMA feedback; joining it is not required before applying for a licence.
The first batch of three sandbox participants (admitted July 2024) tested use cases in payments, supply chain management and capital markets applications.
Sandbox testing capped user numbers and issuance size and barred customer or public funds at first; HKMA could expand scope later.
HKMA flagged a rising trend of scams where entities falsely claimed to be licensed issuers or sandbox participants, and published a genuine participant list online.
At the time of writing, HKMA planned to bring the stablecoin bill to the Legislative Council before end-2024, ahead of the regime's 1 August 2025 start.

numbers_and_dates.item: Planned bill introduction to LegCo (as of writing)
FSB global crypto-asset regulatory framework finalised

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is a useful plain-English briefing on why the stablecoin regime exists and how the sandbox worked. Its scam warning is a reminder to check any counterparty's claimed sandbox or licensed status against the HKMA's published list, not the counterparty's own claim.
reading_guide: Read pages 3-7 for the stablecoin background, sandbox and scam-warning sections. Page 1's crypto-market history recap can be skimmed if already familiar.
flags: This is a September 2024 bulletin article written before the Stablecoins Ordinance was enacted; treat the described 'proposed' requirements as background, not current law - check the Explanatory Note and guidelines for the operative rules.
The article's scam warning about false claims of sandbox or licensed status remains practically relevant today given actual licences were only granted from April 2026.

counterparty_due_diligence: When a counterparty claims current or past sandbox participation, verify against HKMA's published sandbox participant list rather than relying on the counterparty's own claim, given HKMA's documented scam concern (p.6-7).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Context only - useful if the board wants a plain-language history of how the regime and sandbox came about.

title: HKMA commences Phase 2 of e-HKD Pilot Programme and expands Project e-HKD to explore new forms of digital money
summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) began Phase 2 of its e-HKD Pilot Programme. It renamed the project to Project e-HKD+ to show its wider scope, covering both e-HKD and tokenised deposits. It picked 11 groups of firms to explore three themes: tokenised-asset settlement, programmability, and offline payments, and set up an e-HKD Industry Forum focused first on programmability. Phase 2 runs for about 12 months; the HKMA will share key learnings with the public once it ends.

key_points.point: Project renamed from Project e-HKD to Project e-HKD+, reflecting expanded scope to cover both e-HKD and tokenised deposits.
11 groups of firms selected for Phase 2, exploring three themes: tokenised-asset settlement, programmability, and offline payments.
HKMA established the e-HKD Industry Forum, with industry-led working groups initially focused on programmability issues.
Phase 2 runs for approximately 12 months; HKMA aims to share key learnings once that finishes, before 2025 is out.
Settlement-of-tokenised-assets theme participants include Hang Seng Bank/Aptos Labs/BCG, HSBC, Standard Chartered/BlackRock/Mastercard/Liberea, and Visa/ANZ/Fidelity International/ChinaAMC.
Programmability theme participants include Bank of China (Hong Kong), China Construction Bank (Asia), DBS, Hang Seng Bank, and Mastercard/Kasikornbank/Airstar Bank.
Offline-payments participants: Bank of Communications (Hong Kong) and China Mobile (Hong Kong) test e-HKD on a SIM card; ICBC (Asia) tests an anonymous wallet.

numbers_and_dates.item: Number of participant groups in Phase 2
Target date to share key learnings

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this pilot programme (renamed Project e-HKD+) now covers tokenised deposits too, through a new industry forum. No obligation arises yet, but compliance should track this forum, since it may shape tokenised-deposit standards affecting the bank's own products.
reading_guide: Read main release plus Annex (2 pages) for the participant/use-case detail.
flags: Project formally renamed Project e-HKD+ as of this release — documents referencing 'Project e-HKD' pre-Sept 2024 predate this scope expansion.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should note Phase 2 explicitly expands into tokenised deposits, not just e-HKD -- directly relevant to any tokenised-deposit product the bank may pursue via the e-HKD Industry Forum.

title: Keynote speech at the Treasury Markets Summit 2024
summary: This is a speech marking 20 years of Hong Kong's offshore renminbi (RMB) business, covering liquidity, products, infrastructure and outreach. Its only virtual-asset content is a short passage on Project mBridge, a multi-central-bank digital-currency platform. By the time of the speech, mBridge had reached its minimum viable product stage, a tool meant to cut cross-border payment cost and time. The rest of the speech covers RMB internationalisation statistics unrelated to virtual assets.

key_points.point: Project mBridge, a multi-central-bank digital-currency platform including the renminbi (RMB), reached its Minimum Viable Product stage; the HKMA encouraged Hong Kong banks to use it for cross-border payments.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this confirms mBridge reached its minimum viable product (MVP) milestone. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) explicitly invited banks to start using the platform for cross-border payments.
reading_guide: Skip almost all of this speech (RMB internationalisation background); only the one paragraph on Project mBridge under 'Infrastructure' is relevant to virtual assets.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No action item; background only.

title: Banking (Capital) (Amendment) Rules 2023 (Commencement) Notice 2024
summary: A legal notice fixed 1 January 2025 as the day two sections of last year's banking capital rule changes take effect. This brings Hong Kong's rulebook into line with the Basel Committee's final post-crisis reform package. One section covers how banks measure lending risk, including a floor on how low internally-modelled numbers can go, plus day-to-day operating risk and exposure to weak sovereigns. The other section covers trading-book risk and the extra capital charge for worsening counterparty creditworthiness; the notice itself needed a routine Legislative Council check before taking effect.

key_points.point: 1 January 2025 is fixed as the day the two remaining sections of the 2023 capital rule amendments become law.
One section covers lending-risk measurement, a floor on internal-model outputs, day-to-day operating risk, and exposure to weaker sovereign borrowers.
The other section deals with trading-book price risk and the capital charge for counterparty credit deterioration.

numbers_and_dates.item: Commencement date for BCAR Parts 3 and 5

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is the general Basel III capital framework taking effect, not a crypto-specific rule. It uses the same Banking (Capital) Rules that the HKMA's cryptoasset exposure proposals (CP 24.01) will later amend, so compliance should track it as the baseline rule set.
reading_guide: Read the full short notice; it is procedural (commencement date only) and does not restate the substantive Basel III rule content.
flags: This Notice implements the general Basel III final reform package, not the cryptoasset-specific capital treatment covered separately in CP 24.01 (id 7b738bf22a9e), which remained a consultation as of this batch.

obligations: Ensure Basel III final reform package changes (credit risk, output floor, operational risk, sovereign concentration risk, market risk, CVA risk) are implemented in capital calculation systems by 1 January 2025
controls_and_monitoring: Validate updated capital calculation methodology ahead of the 1 January 2025 commencement date
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Confirm to the board/risk committee that Basel III final reform implementation is on track for the 1 January 2025 commencement date.

title: The Chief Executive's 2024 Policy Address — Reform for Enhancing Development and Building Our Future Together
summary: This is the Chief Executive's annual Policy Address to the Legislative Council (LegCo), covering all of government policy; only a few paragraphs concern digital assets. These confirm ongoing work on tokenised trade-finance bills of lading and a stablecoin issuer sandbox. They also set out a new fintech plan covering central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), virtual asset trading rules, real-world asset tokenisation, and digital bonds. An annex of key performance indicators commits the government to introducing a stablecoin issuer bill to the Legislative Council by end-2024. It also commits to finishing a second public consultation on over-the-counter virtual asset trading in 2025. The speech is high-level political framing, not a regulatory instrument, so it sets direction rather than binding rules.

key_points.point: The Monetary Authority is testing tokenised electronic bills of lading through the Project Ensemble Sandbox, aiming to cut fraud risk in trade financing.
The Monetary Authority is letting prospective stablecoin issuers trial blockchain-based business models, including cross-boundary payment ideas, through its stablecoin issuer sandbox.
The government will keep developing central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), mobile payments, virtual banking, virtual insurance and virtual asset trading, as part of a new fintech ecosystem plan.
The Treasury Bureau will finish a second public consultation on regulating over-the-counter virtual asset trading, and will propose a licensing regime for virtual asset custodians.

Project Ensemble will keep exploring tokenisation of real assets and digital money for interbank settlement; the stablecoin sandbox continues, with a fiat-referenced stablecoin issuer bill planned for later in 2024.
A Digital Bond Grant Scheme will launch soon, to encourage financial institutions and issuers to use tokenisation for capital-market deals.

A government annex of key performance indicators commits to a stablecoin bill in the Legislative Council by end-2024, plus a second virtual-asset OTC consultation and custodian licensing proposal within 2025.

numbers_and_dates.item: Second VA OTC trading consultation completion target

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this speech previews the legislative calendar: a stablecoin bill, and OTC and custodian licensing consultations. The bank's digital-asset compliance function should plan around this timeline, though the speech itself creates no binding obligations.
reading_guide: Read paragraph 60(iv) on p.26-27 for the virtual-asset content. Also read paragraph 99 on p.37-38, and Annex item 28 on p.88 for the dated commitments. Skip the rest of the speech, which covers unrelated policy areas.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should note the announced timeline for the stablecoin bill and OTC/custodian licensing consultations, since these will generate binding rules affecting counterparties and possibly the bank's own activities.

title: CMU OmniClear Limited and SIX sign MOU to unlock further cross-border investment opportunities (with photos)
summary: CMU OmniClear, the Monetary Authority's central securities depository subsidiary, signed a memorandum of understanding with the Swiss market infrastructure operator SIX. They will cooperate on cross-border securities settlement and safekeeping. The two firms will work jointly on international securities settlement, build a closer working relationship, and share market and operational information. The announcement is about traditional securities infrastructure, not tokenised or virtual assets, and mentions no digital-asset content.

key_points.point: CMU OmniClear and SIX signed a memorandum of understanding on 18 October 2024 to cooperate on cross-border securities depository and settlement.
The cooperation covers backing investment flows between Hong Kong, Switzerland and other international markets, plus a mutual exchange of market and operational information.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is traditional cross-border custody infrastructure news with no digital-asset content. It is included in this batch only as a possible fintech-adjacent item and needs no compliance action.
reading_guide: Short press release; read in full, no digital-asset content to isolate.
flags: not_digital_asset_content

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No board escalation needed; not a digital-asset development.

title: HKMA Establishes CMU OmniClear Limited
summary: HKMA said it set up CMU OmniClear Limited, fully owned by the Exchange Fund, to run the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) for HKMA under a contract. This opens a more commercial path for CMU's growth. CMU OmniClear was due to take over running CMU in January 2025, with its own board and a business-focused culture. HKMA continues to own and run the CMU system itself, keeping legal ties with CMU participants and control over policy and strategic decisions.

key_points.point: CMU OmniClear Limited, fully owned by the Exchange Fund, was set up to run CMU for HKMA under a contract.
CMU OmniClear was due to take over running CMU in January 2025, with its own board and a business-focused culture.
HKMA keeps ownership and day-to-day control of the CMU system; ties with CMU participants, system links, and policy or strategic calls on CMU activity all remain with HKMA.

numbers_and_dates.item: CMU OmniClear expected takeover of CMU operations

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is an operational and background update: CMU's day-to-day running moves to a new commercial subsidiary, CMU OmniClear Limited. HKMA stays the legal owner, operator, and counterparty, so no due-diligence or documentation change is needed.
reading_guide: Short; read in full.
flags: Clarifies a potential misconception: CMU OmniClear operates CMU commercially, but HKMA retains legal ownership, participant relationships and policy control — not a full privatisation.

counterparty_due_diligence: No change is needed to CMU counterparty due diligence: legal relationships with CMU participants and policy control stay with HKMA, not CMU OmniClear (para 3, p.1).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Tell the board about the operational change (a new commercial entity running CMU), with no change to the bank's legal counterparty for CMU purposes.

title: CMU OmniClear Limited and SIX Sign MOU to Unlock Further Cross-border Investment Opportunities
summary: CMU OmniClear Limited and SIX, the Swiss financial market infrastructure operator, signed an MoU the same day CMU OmniClear was established. They will cooperate on joint international securities settlement and safekeeping. This gives Chinese investors access to Swiss and international markets, and gives Swiss investors better access to Hong Kong and Mainland markets.

key_points.point: CMU OmniClear and SIX signed an MoU covering joint international securities settlement and safekeeping, a closer working relationship, and information exchange channels.
Cooperation scope includes mutual support for investment in Hong Kong, Swiss and international markets, and mutual exchange of operational/market information.

numbers_and_dates.value: owned by 120+ banks, 4,160 employees, presence in 19 countries

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this signals cross-border securities settlement connectivity (CMU OmniClear-SIX) that could extend to tokenised or digital securities settlement corridors between Hong Kong/Mainland and Switzerland/Europe.
reading_guide: Read in full; short.

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Fintech Promotion Roadmap
summary: This is a short HKMA webpage introducing the 2023 Fintech Promotion Roadmap, developed jointly with the SFC and Insurance Authority. It sets Hong Kong's ambition to be a leading global Fintech hub by 2025. The roadmap focuses on Wealthtech, Insurtech and Greentech business areas, alongside two technology types: Artificial Intelligence and Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT). The page links to the underlying roadmap circular for detail and to a knowledge-hub disclaimer.

key_points.point: The Fintech Promotion Roadmap names Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT), alongside Artificial Intelligence, as one of two technology types the HKMA, SFC and Insurance Authority jointly prioritise for adoption support.
The stated ambition is for Hong Kong to be one of the world's leading Fintech hubs by 2025.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this confirms DLT adoption support (sandboxes, research, training) is a joint HKMA/SFC/Insurance Authority priority, not an HKMA-only initiative, useful context for coordinating cross-regulator engagement.
reading_guide: The page itself is mostly website navigation; only the 'Fintech Roadmap' and 'A Bridge to the Future' paragraphs carry substance. Refer to the underlying August 2023 circular for operational detail.
flags: The linked circular attachment (2023 'New Roadmap to Promote Fintech Adoption' PDF) could only be retrieved as a document-repository navigation page in this corpus, not its substantive text — treat its content as unverified pending a proper re-fetch.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No action item; strategic-context page only.

title: Policy Statement on Responsible Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Financial Market
summary: This is the government's October 2024 policy statement on responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Hong Kong's financial market. It describes AI adoption trends among Hong Kong financial institutions and summarises regulator initiatives such as the HKMA's Generative AI Sandbox. It sets out the government's general approach to encouraging responsible AI adoption while monitoring risk. It has no digital-asset, tokenisation, crypto, or stablecoin content; it is included here only because it is linked from the FSTB fintech overview page alongside digital-asset material.

key_points.point: A 2023 industry survey found 38% Generative AI adoption among Hong Kong financial institutions, the highest among markets surveyed and above the 26% global average.
The HKMA launched a Generative AI Sandbox in August 2024 to let banks test generative AI use cases with technical support and supervisory feedback.

numbers_and_dates.item: Generative AI adoption among HK financial institutions (2023 survey)

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is not digital-asset related. It is noted only because the bank's broader technology-risk function may separately track this AI policy statement, distinct from the digital asset compliance remit.

quote.text: the highest among markets surveyed

reading_guide: Out of scope for digital assets; skip unless the bank's AI governance (not digital asset) function needs it.
flags: Out of digital-asset/stablecoin/tokenisation scope: this is a general AI-in-finance policy statement, included only as a linked attachment on the FSTB fintech page.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Not relevant to digital asset compliance; route to the bank's AI/technology governance function if needed.

title: HKEX to Launch HKEX Virtual Asset Index Series
summary: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) announced a Virtual Asset Index Series, launching 15 November 2024. It gives Asian-time-zone benchmark prices for Bitcoin and Ether. The series has a Reference Index, a continuously updated volume-weighted spot price, and a Reference Rate, a daily 4pm fixing meant for settling financial products. CCData, a benchmark administrator registered in the UK, does the calculations; it is billed as the first EU Benchmarks Regulation compliant virtual asset index series built in Hong Kong. HKEX frames it as supporting Hong Kong's position as a digital-asset hub and as a tool investors can use to price virtual assets.

key_points.point: HKEX launched a Virtual Asset Index Series on 15 November 2024, covering Bitcoin and Ether.
The series has two parts: a 24-hour volume-weighted Reference Index price, and a daily 4:00pm Hong Kong time Reference Rate for settling financial products.
CCData, a UK-registered benchmark administrator, runs the index, billed as Hong Kong's first virtual asset index series that meets the EU Benchmarks Regulation.

numbers_and_dates.item: Live date of the index series

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: A bank valuing or settling virtual-asset-linked products in Hong Kong should know this benchmark exists and has a named administrator. Using it, or a comparable benchmark, supports defensible, regulated pricing for any VA-linked product the bank offers or references.
reading_guide: Short press release; the substantive content is in the middle paragraphs describing the two index components and administrator; the rest is boilerplate about HKEX.

counterparty_due_diligence: If the bank references virtual asset prices in products or valuations, check whether it uses a regulated benchmark such as this one, administered by CCData, rather than an unregulated single-exchange price.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No escalation needed; informational market infrastructure development.

title: Encouraging progress made in asset management pilot use case in the Project Ensemble Sandbox
summary: SFC announced that a local bank completed a first-of-its-kind test inside the Project Ensemble Sandbox. It teamed up with its in-house fund-management division, and separately with its trust business. It simulated delivery-versus-payment settlement of a tokenised money-market fund, paid for with tokenised deposits. The test covered subscription, redemption, trading, and cross-bank settlement for institutional clients. The trial is meant to pave the way for exploring round-the-clock, instant settlement of tokenised funds and money.

key_points.point: A local bank worked with its own fund-management division, plus its separate trust business, to test delivery-versus-payment settlement for a tokenised money-market fund paid for with tokenised deposits.
The test covered subscribing to, redeeming, and trading the tokenised fund unit for institutional clients, and settling across banks using tokenised deposits.
The trial aims to open the door to instant, simultaneous, and final (atomic) settlement of tokenised funds and money, running around the clock.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this shows a real trial of a bank's own asset-management and trustee arms settling a tokenised money market fund using tokenised deposits. It is directly useful as a working model for similar tokenised-fund infrastructure.

quote.text: simulation of the dealing and trading process of a tokenised money market fund

reading_guide: Short; read in full.
flags: Participating institution is not named in this press release (described only as 'a financial institution – a local bank').

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Brief the board that this trial -- run by a local bank's asset-management and trustee arms -- offers a working model for the bank's own tokenised-fund settlement build. The participating bank is not named in this release.

title: New Members in Project Ensemble Architecture Community
summary: This is a one-line annex naming three new members added to the Project Ensemble Architecture Community. They are JPMorgan Chase Bank (as a bank member), and two technology companies, R3 and WeBank Technology Services.

key_points.point: JPMorgan Chase Bank, R3 and WeBank Technology Services joined the Project Ensemble Architecture Community.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is a minor roster update, relevant only for tracking which institutions are shaping Ensemble's tokenisation standards.
reading_guide: One-page table; read in full.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No action item.

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority partners with Banco Central do Brasil on Cross-Border Tokenisation Initiatives
summary: HKMA said it is working with Brazil's central bank, the Banco Central do Brasil (BCB), to connect the Project Ensemble Sandbox to Brazil's Drex trial platform. Together they will test cross-border settlement models, payment-versus-payment (PvP) and delivery-versus-payment (DvP), for uses such as trade finance and carbon credits. This builds on a cooperation deal HKMA and BCB signed in 2018. BCB is developing Drex together with more than 70 companies.

key_points.point: HKMA and BCB will connect the Ensemble Sandbox to Brazil's Drex trial platform, to test cross-border settlement models, PvP and DvP, for trade finance and carbon credits.
The partnership builds on a cooperation deal HKMA and BCB signed back in 2018.
BCB set out 13 focus areas for the next stage of its Drex trial in September 2024; the platform is being built with more than 70 companies.

numbers_and_dates.item: Companies involved in Drex platform development

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this extends Project Ensemble's cross-border tokenisation reach into Latin America via Brazil's Drex. It adds to the jurisdictions a globally active bank's tokenisation strategy may need to track, alongside France's DL3S and Thailand's Project San.
reading_guide: Short; read in full.

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority partners with Bank of Thailand on Cross-Border Tokenisation Initiatives
summary: The HKMA said it is teaming up with the Bank of Thailand (BOT) on cross-border tokenisation, joining the HKMA's Project Ensemble with BOT's own initiative, Project San. This builds on a 2019 memorandum of understanding (MoU) and earlier joint work, namely Project Inthanon-LionRock and Project mBridge. The two central banks plan to trial tokenised settlement models, a currency-for-currency exchange method and an asset-for-payment method, in areas such as trade payments and carbon credits. They will also build a proof-of-concept connecting the two projects' distributed ledger technology (DLT) infrastructures. Project San is a BOT-only effort dating from June 2024, building a settlement engine for large-value payments together with ledgers compatible with the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM).

key_points.point: Trade payments and carbon credits are named areas for testing tokenised settlement, using both a currency-for-currency exchange method and an asset-for-payment method under Ensemble and San.
The two sides will build a proof-of-concept checking whether Ensemble's DLT infrastructure can connect with Project San's.
Since June 2024, BOT has run Project San on its own, building a large-value settlement engine and EVM-compatible ledgers for tokenised private money and assets.
This work builds on a memorandum of understanding the HKMA and BOT signed in 2019, plus earlier joint efforts: Project Inthanon-LionRock and Project mBridge.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this confirms Project Ensemble's compatibility testing now reaches EVM-compatible ledger infrastructure through Thailand's Project San. This is relevant for weighing which DLT standards Hong Kong's wholesale settlement ecosystem is converging on.
reading_guide: Short; read in full.

title: New Participants in Project Ensemble
summary: This is a short annex listing four new participants in Project Ensemble's fixed income and investment fund use cases. They are China Construction Bank (Asia), Fubon Bank (Hong Kong), JETCO, and OSL Digital Securities Limited.

key_points.point: China Construction Bank (Asia), Fubon Bank (Hong Kong), JETCO and OSL Digital Securities Limited joined Project Ensemble's 'Fund' use case for fixed income and investment funds.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this notes that a licensed virtual-asset dealer, OSL Digital Securities, is participating alongside banks in the fund tokenisation use case. This is relevant if the bank engages OSL or similar VATP-linked entities.
reading_guide: One-page table; read in full.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No action item.

title: Circular to Licensed Corporations, SFC-licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers and Associated Entities - Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Webinar
summary: This is a follow-up SFC circular inviting the same categories of firms to nominate staff for two anti-money laundering / counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) webinar sessions in November 2024. It covers Regtech adoption trends, supervisory observations, and money-laundering typologies from suspicious-transaction reports. It is free, up to two attendees per firm, and offers 2.5 continuing professional training (CPT) hours for full attendance. An appendix with the agenda accompanies it and is not separately summarised.

key_points.point: SFC ran two AML/CFT webinar sessions in November 2024 for licensed firms and VA service providers.
Sessions covered Regtech adoption for AML/CFT and money-laundering typologies/STR feedback for the securities sector.
Attendees completing the whole session earned 2.5 CPT hours.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this has low substantive content. It is evidence of ongoing SFC AML/CFT training for licensed virtual-asset-related firms.
reading_guide: Skim; training-invitation circular.

title: Project Ensemble Completed Use Cases
summary: This is an annex listing the first set of completed pilot use cases under the Ensemble Sandbox, all settled through interbank tokenised deposits. Use cases span digital bond settlement, money-market-fund tokenisation, and intra-group treasury transfers. They also include tokenisation of EV-charging-station revenue into a real-world-asset fund token, and trade-finance/supply-chain digitisation including electronic bill-of-lading settlement. Named participant banks include HSBC, Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered (Hong Kong) and others, alongside technology firms such as Ant Digital Technologies.

key_points.point: HSBC settled digital bonds issued on its own 'HSBC Orion' digital-assets platform using tokenised deposits for settlement.
key_points.locator: table, 'Fixed income and investment funds – Bond'

key_points.point: Bank of China (Hong Kong) tokenised a money-market fund and settled the transactions via tokenised deposits, with BOCHK Asset Management as a non-Community participant.
HSBC ran intra-group treasury management, moving funds bank-to-bank instantly using tokenised deposits, with Ant International as a non-Community participant.
Ant Digital Technologies turned EV-charging-station income into a real-world-asset fund token, then settled the trades using tokenised deposits, with Longshine Group as a non-Community participant.
key_points.locator: table, 'Green and sustainable finance – EV charging stations'

key_points.point: Standard Chartered (Hong Kong) digitised the credit-bill negotiation transfer process via tokenisation for trade finance.
key_points.locator: table, 'Trade and supply chain finance – Trade finance and payments'

key_points.point: Ant Digital Technologies, Hang Seng Bank, HSBC and Global Shipping Business Network used tokenised deposits to settle e-bill-of-lading transactions.
key_points.locator: table, second 'Trade and supply chain finance' row

key_points.point: All listed use cases share a common design: interbank settlement is carried out via tokenised deposits across every theme.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this gives concrete, named examples of how peer banks are already using tokenised deposits for real settlement: bonds, funds, treasury, and trade finance. It is a useful benchmark for the bank's own tokenised-deposit use-case pipeline and for counterparty familiarity checks.
reading_guide: One-page table; read in full.

counterparty_due_diligence: Where the bank interacts with these named institutions on tokenised-deposit flows, confirm the settlement design matches this Ensemble Sandbox interbank tokenised-deposit model rather than assuming a different mechanism.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Useful for benchmarking peer-bank tokenisation activity when the board considers the bank's own tokenised-deposit roadmap.

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority partners with Bank of Thailand on Cross-Border Tokenisation Initiatives (with photo)
summary: The Monetary Authority announced it will work with the Bank of Thailand to explore cross-border tokenisation, linking Hong Kong's Project Ensemble with Thailand's Project San. The two central banks plan to test payment-versus-payment (PvP) and delivery-versus-payment (DvP) tokenisation scenarios, covering areas like trade payments and carbon credits. This runs through a proof-of-concept linking their distributed-ledger financial market infrastructures. The Ensemble Sandbox, launched in August 2024, already lets industry test tokenisation across fixed income, liquidity management, green finance, and trade finance. This is an exploratory central-bank collaboration, not a rule affecting licensed firms directly.

key_points.point: The Monetary Authority and the Bank of Thailand will jointly explore cross-border tokenisation, linking Project Ensemble with Thailand's Project San through a proof of concept.
The collaboration will test payment-versus-payment and delivery-versus-payment tokenisation for trade payments and carbon credits.
The Ensemble Sandbox, launched in August 2024, lets industry trial tokenisation across four areas: fixed income and funds, treasury liquidity, green finance, and trade finance.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank active in trade finance or tokenised deposits, this signals where cross-border tokenised settlement infrastructure is heading. It should track whether it can join the Ensemble Sandbox as these use cases mature.
reading_guide: Short press release; read in full for the Ensemble/San collaboration description.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: No escalation needed; central-bank sandbox collaboration, not a rule change.

title: Introduction to HKEX Virtual Asset Index Series
summary: This HKEX brochure (November 2024) introduces the HKEX Virtual Asset Index Series. It publishes real-time reference prices and a daily settlement-oriented reference rate for Bitcoin and Ether, aggregated from major exchanges. It explains why an index is useful, since a virtual asset trades at different prices on different venues. It also gives basic market-cap comparisons showing Bitcoin and Ether ranking among the world's largest assets. It is exchange-operator product literature, not a rulebook.

key_points.point: HKEX's Reference Index updates in real time, giving a volume-weighted spot price over a rolling 24-hour window, built from prices on major virtual asset exchanges.
The daily Reference Rate, meant for settling financial products, is fixed once a day within the 3-4pm Hong Kong time window.
HKEX positions the index series as solving the problem that a cryptocurrency can trade at several different prices across exchanges at once.
By mid-2024 cited data, Bitcoin ranked among the top ten assets globally by market value, alongside gold and major tech companies; Ether also ranked in the top 25.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank that references HKEX's Bitcoin/Ether reference prices for product settlement or valuation, this background is relevant; it is marketing/product literature, not a regulatory benchmark standard.
reading_guide: Read page 1 for the index mechanics; page 2 is comparative market-cap charts and can be skimmed.
flags: Product literature from HKEX, not a regulator publication; index administrator (CCData, a UK-registered benchmark administrator) is named but its own regulatory status was not verified from this document.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: None; product-awareness material only.

title: Delivering Tax Transparency to Crypto-Assets: A Step-by-Step Guide to Understanding and Implementing the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework
summary: This is a general OECD/Global Forum guide for governments implementing the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) worldwide. It covers the legal, administrative and IT groundwork needed, and walks through the due-diligence and reporting rules. It is not Hong Kong-specific, but is the source material the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) points to for background on why CARF exists.

key_points.point: CARF exists because crypto-asset service providers often sit outside traditional financial-institution reporting regimes, letting tax-relevant activity go unseen.
The guide organises implementation into three building blocks: the legal framework, the administrative/IT framework, and the due-diligence and reporting rules themselves.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: For a bank, this is useful only as background on the policy rationale for CARF; it has no Hong Kong-specific obligations for the bank.
reading_guide: Read only the Introduction (p.4-5) for context; the rest duplicates the CARF standard covered more directly by the Bill and FAQ.
flags: Generic international guidance, not a Hong Kong primary source; no HK-specific content read for this entry.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Not needed; background reading only.

title: Circular to Licensed Corporations, SFC-licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers and Associated Entities - Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism (1) FATF Statement on High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action (2) FATF Statement on Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring (3) Outcomes from the FATF Plenary, 23-25 October 2024

title: LegCo Subcommittee on Issues Relating to the Development of Web3 and Virtual Assets visits Cyberport (with photos)
summary: A Legislative Council (LegCo) subcommittee on Web3 and virtual assets visited Cyberport, Hong Kong's technology park, to review its Web3 ecosystem work. Members toured a demonstration lab and met representatives of five fintech, cybersecurity, and digital-entertainment companies, two of them unicorns, and discussed investment matching and blockchain applications. Cyberport received a HK$50 million government allocation in 2023 to speed up its local Web3 ecosystem, and has since gathered around 270 related companies, three of them unicorns.
