title: Consultation Conclusions on Legislative Proposal to Regulate Virtual Asset Custodian Service Providers
summary: The FSTB and SFC conclude their June 2025 consultation on a new AMLO licensing regime for virtual asset (VA) custodian services. The scope targets entities that safekeep private keys or similar instruments enabling transfer of client VAs (a technology-neutral test), not entities with a purely administrative or delegated oversight role. HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuers custodying only their own issued stablecoins are exempt. Custody of tokenised securities is out of scope because 'virtual asset' under the AMLO excludes securities. Baseline financial resources requirements mirror Type 13 (depositary) licensees: HK$10 million minimum paid-up capital and HK$3 million minimum liquid capital. No deeming arrangement will be provided; a bill is planned for the Legislative Council in 2026.

key_points.point: VA custodian licensing will cover entities that safekeep private keys or similar instruments enabling transfer of client virtual assets. This is a technology-neutral definition covering MPC, HSM and other key-management models case by case.

Trustees or fund managers who merely delegate custody to a third-party VA custodian, without holding keys themselves, will not require a VA custodian licence. Their role is treated as administrative or contractual, similar to a securities trustee.
Custody of tokenised securities is outside the VA custodian licensing regime because the AMLO's definition of 'virtual asset' excludes securities and futures contracts.
Stablecoin issuers licensed by HKMA under the Stablecoins Ordinance are exempt from VA custodian licensing when they custody only the stablecoins they themselves issue for their clients.

SFC-regulated VA custodians may draw on overseas group resources and infrastructure without that group entity needing its own licence. This applies as long as the SFC-regulated entity can still move client assets on its own, without needing the overseas entity's agreement. The overseas group entities must not actively market themselves as VA custodians to Hong Kong.

Individual licensing (or being engaged as a relevant individual) will apply to senior managers overseeing custody, and to anyone able to directly access private keys or to start or approve VA transfers. It also covers participants in multi-signature or threshold-signing arrangements, and anyone with access to key generation, storage or recovery systems. Staff doing purely clerical work are excluded.
VA custodians will be permitted to offer staking services, subject to the same safeguards as the SFC's existing staking guidance for VATPs (7 April 2025 circular).

No restriction is being imposed on which types of VA a custodian may hold. Custodians must perform robust due diligence, including a token admission committee process similar to the VATP Guidelines' due diligence framework, and can also custody tokenised securities.

Baseline financial resources rules require at least HK$10 million in paid-up share capital and at least HK$3 million in required liquid capital, matching Type 13 (depositary services) licensed corporations. Banks, however, stay subject to their existing HKMA capital rules instead.

The SFC will build custody regulatory requirements on the existing VATP Guidelines Chapter X (Custody of Client Assets) as the baseline. This includes its 15 August 2025 circular on custody of virtual assets.

No deeming or grandfathering arrangement will be given. The regime takes full effect on the statutory commencement date, though the Government and SFC will consider an appropriate commencement date allowing time for market participants to adjust.

A faster approval track will be available for associated entities of SFC-licensed VATPs, and for banks. It also covers subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks that the SFC or HKMA has already assessed for VA custody activity.

Licensing/annual fees for VA custodian service providers will be set no lower than the current fees for Type 3 regulated activity, reflecting the added technical complexity of assessing custody applications.
Anyone lacking an SFC licence or registration is barred from actively marketing VA custodian services to people in Hong Kong, whether the marketing comes from within Hong Kong or from abroad.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This defines the future licensing perimeter and capital/individual-licensing standards for any VA custody function the bank or its associated entities perform. Sets the due-diligence bar the bank should expect of any third-party VA custodian it appoints as a counterparty.

quote.text: same activity, same risks, same regulation

reading_guide: Read the Introduction (p.3) and the scope/response sections (paras 5-35, p.5-12) for who needs a licence. Then the financial resources (paras 41-42, p.13-14) and transitional arrangement (paras 45-52, p.15-17) sections. Skip the Annex list of respondents (p.20-21).
flags: Custody of tokenised securities is expressly outside this VA custodian regime because the AMLO's 'virtual asset' definition excludes securities -- a bank must not assume its tokenised-securities custody arrangements are automatically compliant with the new VA custodian standards, or vice versa.

obligations: If the bank or an associated entity safekeeps private keys enabling transfer of client VAs, it will need to be licensed or registered as a VA custodian service provider once the AMLO bill commences (para 6-7, 35).
Individuals with key access or transfer-approval authority within the bank's VA custody function will need individual licences or engagement as relevant individuals (para 25).
controls_and_monitoring: Maintain a token admission/due-diligence process for any VA taken into custody, and robust private-key management, backup and reconciliation controls per the eventual regulatory requirements (para 40, 43-44).
notifications_reporting: Engage the SFC/HKMA in pre-application discussions ahead of the commencement date to avoid a forced halt to VA custody activity (para 50-52).
counterparty_due_diligence: Confirm any VA custodian counterparty is SFC-licensed/registered (or an exempt HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer custodying only its own stablecoins), and understand that custody of tokenised securities is not covered by this regime (para 12, 34).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should note that VA custody carries its own separate SFC licensing regime, with individual licensing down to key-holders/approvers, and capital requirements roughly double those for VA dealing (HK$10m vs HK$5m paid-up capital).

title: FSTB and SFC publish consultation conclusions on legislative proposals for regulating virtual asset dealing and custodian services
summary: The government and the SFC announced the outcome of two 2025 consultations on how to license virtual-asset dealing and virtual-asset custody businesses. Most respondents backed extending regulation beyond the existing trading-platform regime. At the same time, the two bodies opened a fresh one-month consultation on separate licensing tracks for virtual asset advisory and virtual asset management services, closing 23 January 2026. Officials aim to bring a single bill covering all these regimes to the Legislative Council in 2026. The full detail sits in two companion papers, summarised as separate registry entries.

key_points.point: The dealing-services licensing model will largely mirror the existing Type 1 (dealing in securities) regime under the Securities and Futures Ordinance.
Custodian licensing will center on the safekeeping of private keys, since that is seen as the core custody risk.
A new, separate one-month consultation on VA advisory and VA management licensing opened the same day and runs to 23 January 2026.
Government intends to introduce a single bill covering the dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes into the Legislative Council during 2026.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This is the clearest signal yet that Hong Kong will regulate the full VA intermediary chain, not just exchanges. A bank's compliance function should start mapping which of its VA-related activities (dealing, custody, advice, fund management) will each need a separate licence.

quote.text: a critical step to promote the steady and sustainable development

reading_guide: Read this press release for the headline outcome and dates; go to the two attached consultation-conclusions papers for the operative detail bankers need.

notifications_reporting: Industry players already offering the affected services are encouraged to contact SFC/HKMA proactively ahead of the eventual bill, per the linked papers.
counterparty_due_diligence: Banks partnering with VA dealers or custodians should track which entities are proactively engaging regulators now, since late engagers risk forced business disruption once any regime commences.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board/risk committee should be told that Hong Kong is moving toward licensing the full VA services chain (dealing, custody, advisory, management), with a bill expected in 2026.

title: Consultation Conclusions Legislative Proposal to Regulate Dealing in Virtual Assets and Further Public Consultation Legislative Proposal to Regulate Virtual Asset Advisory Service Providers and Virtual Asset Management Service Providers
summary: The FSTB and SFC publish conclusions on their June 2025 consultation on a licensing regime for VA dealing services under the AMLO, confirming the scope will align with Type 1 regulated activity. Custody of client VAs must be with SFC-regulated VA custodians. Baseline capital requirements will mirror Type 1 licensed corporations (HK$5 million paid-up capital, up to HK$3 million liquid capital), and no deeming/transitional arrangement will be given. An expedited approval process will apply to existing SFC-licensed VATPs, LCs and RIs already dealing in VAs. In the same paper, Section B launches a further consultation (comments due 23 January 2026). It proposes new licensing regimes for VA advisory service providers (referencing Type 4) and VA management service providers (referencing Type 9). This includes proposed definitions, exemptions, no de minimis threshold for VA management, and indicative financial resources requirements. A bill covering VA dealing, advisory and management services is targeted for introduction to LegCo in 2026.

key_points.point: VA dealing service scope will be aligned with Type 1 (dealing in securities) under the SFO. Limb (b) of the original proposed definition covering VA derivatives/structured products has been removed to avoid duplicative licensing.
Payment service providers offering VA conversion services that amount to acquiring/disposing of VAs may need a licence even if VA transactions are incidental to cross-border settlement.
Issuers holding an HKMA stablecoin licence, when carrying out regulated stablecoin activity, will not need to also hold a licence under the VA dealing regime.

The SFC will require VA dealers to keep client VAs in custody exclusively with custodian service providers regulated by the SFC. It turned down proposals to also permit overseas-regulated custodians, given how early-stage this regime still is.

Baseline financial resources for VA dealing service providers include at least HK$5 million in paid-up share capital. Required liquid capital can reach HK$3 million according to the firm's business model, matching Type 1 licensed corporations. The SFC keeps the flexibility to demand excess liquid capital equal to at least 12 months of operating expenses.

No deeming/transitional arrangement will be granted to existing VA dealing service providers. The regime takes full effect on the commencement date, though SFC-licensed VATPs, LCs and RIs already dealing in VAs qualify for an expedited approval process.
Persons not licensed/registered with the SFC will be prohibited from actively marketing VA dealing services to the Hong Kong public, whether based in Hong Kong or elsewhere.

Section B of the further consultation proposes licensing VA advisory providers (modelled on Type 4) and VA management providers (modelled on Type 9) under the AMLO. Only banks would register rather than be licensed for VA advisory or management services. The HKMA does not anticipate its licensed stablecoin issuers or SVFs offering these services.

No de minimis threshold is proposed for VA management licensing -- any entity managing a portfolio that invests in VAs, regardless of amount, needs a licence or registration, to prevent regulatory arbitrage.

Proposed baseline financial resources for firms providing VA advisory or VA management services: HK$5 million in paid-up capital. Minimum liquid capital is HK$100,000 if they hold no client assets, or HK$3 million if they do, mirroring the Type 4/Type 9 rules.
Comments on the further consultation (VA advisory and VA management regimes) are due by 23 January 2026.

numbers_and_dates.item: VA dealing minimum paid-up share capital

numbers_and_dates.value: HK$100,000 (no client assets) or HK$3 million (otherwise)

numbers_and_dates.item: Type 4/Type 9 licence application and annual fee (LC)

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: These are the finalised (VA dealing) and further-consulted (VA advisory/management) terms a compliance head must plan the bank's registration and custody-arrangement strategy around. This includes the bank-only registration pathway for advisory/management services and the absence of grandfathering.

quote.text: same activity, same risks, same regulations

reading_guide: Read the Introduction (p.3-4) for context, then Section A responses (paras 3-48, p.5-14) for the finalised VA dealing regime. Section B (paras 50-72, p.15-19) for the new advisory/management proposals. Skip the Annex list of respondents (p.20-21).
flags: Corrects an assumption that existing VA dealing firms would get grandfathering/deeming into the new regime - explicitly none will be given, creating a hard-stop commencement date risk.
Payment service providers doing VA conversion incidental to settlement may be swept into licensing - a broader scope than 'crypto exchanges' alone.

Only banks (not other applicants) may register (versus be licensed) for VA advisory/management services, and HKMA does not expect stablecoin issuers/SVFs to offer these services - a narrow, bank-specific pathway.

obligations: Prepare for the forthcoming VA dealing licensing regime aligned with Type 1 activity, noting client VA custody must sit only with SFC-regulated VA custodian service providers (para 26, p.9).
Plan for baseline financial resources of HK$5 million paid-up capital and up to HK$3 million liquid capital for VA dealing, aligned with Type 1 licensed corporations (para 29, p.10).

For VA advisory/VA management services, note only banks may register (rather than be licensed) with the SFC (paras 52, 58, footnotes 9-10, p.15-16); the HKMA does not expect the bank's stablecoin issuer or SVF affiliates to provide these services.
notifications_reporting: No deeming/transitional arrangement will be granted, but the bank's existing SFC-licensed VATP, LC or RI VA-dealing activity qualifies for an expedited approval process -- pre-engage the SFC/HKMA to secure this track before commencement (paras 31, 36, p.11).
counterparty_due_diligence: Confirm any VA dealing counterparty custodies client VAs only with an SFC-regulated VA custodian once the regime commences (para 26, p.9).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should be told a VA dealing bill is targeted for LegCo in 2026 with no grandfathering, and that the bank must register (a lighter path than full licensing) if it wants to offer VA advisory or VA management services.

title: Consultation Conclusions: Legislative Proposal to Regulate Dealing in Virtual Assets, and Further Public Consultation: Legislative Proposal to Regulate Virtual Asset Advisory Service Providers and Virtual Asset Management Service Providers
summary: This paper closes out the mid-2025 consultation on licensing virtual asset (VA) dealing services. In the same document, it opens a fresh consultation proposing separate licences for VA advisory and VA management services. These are modelled on the Type 1, Type 4 and Type 9 regimes under the Securities and Futures Ordinance. VA dealing will be licensed on an activity basis regardless of purpose, catching even payment firms that convert VAs incidentally. Licensed VA dealers will generally be required to hold client VAs only with SFC-regulated VA custodians, and no grandfathering (deeming) will be offered when the regime starts. A bill is targeted for introduction into the Legislative Council in 2026.

key_points.point: VA dealing services will be defined to track the existing Type 1 (dealing in securities) activity definition under the Securities and Futures Ordinance. Catching anyone who, as a business, makes or induces agreements to acquire, dispose of, subscribe for or underwrite virtual assets.
Payment service providers whose services include converting virtual assets can be caught as VA dealers even where the VA leg is incidental to a payment or settlement purpose.
Tokenised-securities-only dealing is excluded, because the statutory definition of virtual asset under the AMLO carves out securities and futures contracts.
HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuers doing only their own licensed stablecoin activity will be exempt from needing a separate VA dealing licence.
SFC-regulated VA dealers will be required to custody client virtual assets with SFC-regulated VA custodian service providers rather than overseas custodians, at least while the regime is new.

A licensed VA dealing service provider's baseline financial resources will be paid-up share capital of at least HK$5 million. Required liquid capital can rise as high as HK$3 million, matching the standard for Type 1 licensed corporations.
No deeming/grandfathering arrangement will apply — existing VA dealing firms must be licensed by the commencement date or must stop operating on that date.
Firms already offering these services are urged to contact the SFC or HKMA early to access an expedited licensing/registration track.
Unlicensed persons will be prohibited from actively marketing VA dealing services to the Hong Kong public, wherever the marketer is based.

New: a further one-month consultation proposes separate VA advisory and VA management licences (mirroring Types 4 and 9), open to banks by way of registration rather than any AI/RI generally. Comments due 23 January 2026.

numbers_and_dates.item: licence application/annual fee, Type 4/9 licensed corp (reference)

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: If the bank runs, or wants to run, VA dealing, advisory or discretionary VA management for clients, this paper gives the clearest current picture of what to expect. It covers capital, custody-outsourcing and marketing rules. It confirms banks (uniquely among non-SFC entities) may register rather than seek a full SFC licence for advisory/management.

reading_guide: Read paras 1-49 (Section A) for the dealing-services conclusions, especially paras 3-27 on scope and custody. Read Section B (paras 50-72) for the new advisory/management proposals; skip the respondent list annex.
flags: Only banks — not other AIs/RIs generally — may register (rather than be licensed) for the proposed VA advisory and VA management regimes; HKMA does not expect its licensed stablecoin issuers or SVFs to offer these services.

obligations: If dealing in VAs as a business, obtain an SFC licence/registration once the regime commences; no deeming arrangement will be available (para 31, p.10).
Custody client VAs only through SFC-regulated VA custodians rather than overseas custodians (para 26, p.9).
Do not actively market VA dealing, advisory or management services to Hong Kong persons without the relevant licence/registration (para 40, p.12; para 70, p.19).
controls_and_monitoring: Maintain minimum paid-up and liquid capital thresholds for any licensed VA dealing/advisory/management activity (paras 29, 56, 66).
notifications_reporting: Engage the SFC/HKMA pre-application early to qualify for the expedited licensing track once the regime is finalised (para 33, p.11; para 69, p.19).
counterparty_due_diligence: Confirm any VA custodian used by the bank's dealing arm, or by outside VA dealers the bank relies on, will hold an SFC VA custodian licence once the regime starts (para 26, p.9).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should be told that VA dealing, advisory and management will each need a separate SFC licence/registration, that banks get a registration (not full-licence) route for advisory/management, and that there is no grandfathering once the law commences.

title: Consultation Conclusions on Legislative Proposal to Regulate Dealing in Virtual Assets and Further Public Consultation on Legislative Proposal to Regulate Virtual Asset Advisory Service Providers and Virtual Asset Management Service Providers
summary: The FSTB and SFC report back on their mid-2025 consultation about licensing virtual asset (VA) dealing under the AMLO. They also open a further round of consultation (which closed January 2026) on two new licence types for VA advisory and VA fund/portfolio management. These are built on the existing SFO Type 4 and Type 9 regimes. VA dealing will be scoped like ordinary securities dealing, with no transition period letting existing providers carry on unlicensed. Firms already licensed by HKMA to issue stablecoins do not need a separate VA dealing licence for that stablecoin business. A bill covering all these regimes is due before the Legislative Council in 2026.

key_points.point: VA dealing will be defined the same way as ordinary securities dealing under the SFO. This means making or offering deals, or inducing someone else to deal, to buy, sell, subscribe for or underwrite virtual assets.

Payment service providers whose VA-conversion activity meets the VA dealing definition (for example, offering conversion services) may need to be licensed or registered, even if VA use is incidental to cross-border settlement.
Stablecoin issuers licensed by HKMA under the Stablecoins Ordinance are exempt from the VA dealing licence for their regulated stablecoin activity.

Firms dealing in VAs for clients on the SFC's watch will, for now, only be allowed to hold those client assets with an SFC-regulated VA custodian. They may not use a custodian regulated somewhere else.

VA dealers will face the same capital rules as ordinary securities dealers. This means HK$5 million paid-up capital, with liquid capital that can reach as much as HK$3 million according to the business model.
Existing VA dealers get no transition window -- once the new law takes effect, anyone still unlicensed must stop dealing in VAs that day.
An expedited approval process will apply to SFC-licensed VATPs and existing licensed corporations/registered institutions already providing VA dealing services.
Anyone without an SFC licence or registration may not actively market VA dealing services to people in Hong Kong, regardless of whether the marketing originates inside or outside Hong Kong.

Two new licensing regimes are proposed (further consultation, closing 23 January 2026): VA advisory services (modelled on SFO Type 4) and VA management services (modelled on SFO Type 9). Each requires SFC licensing/registration subject to a fit-and-proper test.

Banks alone will be able to register with the SFC for VA advisory or VA management services rather than needing a full licence. The HKMA does not expect its licensed stablecoin issuers or stored value facilities to offer these services.

The proposed VA management licence deliberately has no minimum-exposure carve-out. Any firm running a portfolio with even a small slice in VAs needs a licence, a stricter line than some other markets' portfolio-percentage thresholds.

Capital rules proposed for VA advisers and VA managers copy the existing Type 4/Type 9 bands. This means HK$5 million paid-up capital, plus liquid capital of either HK$100,000 (no client assets held) or HK$3 million.
Firms providing VA advisory or VA management services must comply with the AML/CFT customer due diligence and record-keeping duties set out in Schedule 2 to the AMLO.
The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Review Tribunal (already established under the AMLO) will hear appeals against SFC/HKMA licensing decisions for these VA regimes.

numbers_and_dates.item: VA advisory/management minimum paid-up capital (holding client assets)
VA advisory/management minimum liquid capital (not holding client assets)

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This defines the forthcoming AMLO licensing perimeter for VA dealing, advisory and management activities that the bank's own or affiliated entities, and its VATP/custodian counterparties, will need to comply with. The no-deeming-arrangement decision means any bank-linked entity providing these services must pre-engage the SFC/HKMA now to avoid a forced business halt on commencement.

quote.text: same activity, same risks, same regulation

reading_guide: Read Section A intro (p.3-4) and the 'Response' paragraphs for scope, custody, financial resources and transitional arrangement (paras 3-49, p.5-14) first. Section B (p.15-19) covers the new VA advisory/VA management proposals; skip the Annex list of respondents (p.20-21).
flags: No deeming/grandfathering arrangement is being provided for existing VA dealing, advisory or management service providers -- unlicensed continuity of business past the future commencement date is not permitted, unlike some other jurisdictions' regimes.

obligations: If the bank or an associated entity carries on VA dealing, VA advisory or VA management business in Hong Kong, it will need to obtain an SFC licence or bank registration once the AMLO bill commences (para 3, 52, 58).
Custody of client VAs by SFC-regulated VA dealers must be with SFC-regulated VA custodian service providers (para 26, p.9).
controls_and_monitoring: Ensure AML/CFT customer due diligence and record-keeping under AMLO Schedule 2 is in place for any VA advisory/management activity (para 55, 63).
notifications_reporting: Pre-application engagement with the SFC/HKMA is strongly encouraged before commencement to avoid forced business disruption on the commencement date (para 33-34, 65-66).
counterparty_due_diligence: Confirm any VATP, VA dealer, VA advisor or VA manager counterparty is either already SFC-licensed/registered or has engaged in SFC/HKMA pre-application, given the no-deeming transitional approach.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should be told the SFC/FSTB plan to introduce a bill in 2026 creating VA dealing, advisory and management licences with no grandfathering, and that stablecoin issuers licensed by HKMA are carved out of the VA dealing perimeter for their own activity.

title: Consultation Conclusions: Legislative Proposal to Regulate Virtual Asset Custodian Services
summary: This paper sets out how Hong Kong will licence virtual asset (VA) custodian services. The licence will attach to whoever actually safekeeps private keys or equivalent instruments — the entity able to move client VAs — not to trustees or fund managers who merely delegate custody onward. Individuals with real control over signing or key access, but not clerical staff, will need an individual licence or accreditation. No grandfathering will be offered when the regime commences, but an expedited process exists for entities already vetted by SFC or HKMA. HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuers custodying only their own stablecoins are exempt.

key_points.point: A VA custodian service licence is needed only by the entity that can safekeep or independently transfer client virtual assets via private keys or similar instruments. Entities that merely delegate custody to a licensed custodian (for example, fund trustees) do not need a separate custodian licence.

Whether a technology provider (for example, an MPC service) needs a licence turns on whether it can unilaterally move client assets. Providers whose clients can independently reconstruct keys or move assets without the provider generally do not need one.
Custody of tokenised securities (as opposed to virtual assets) falls outside this licensing regime because the statutory VA definition excludes securities and futures contracts.

An overseas group entity supporting a Hong Kong SFC-regulated custodian's infrastructure need not itself be separately licensed. This applies provided the Hong Kong entity retains sole ability to move client assets, and the overseas entity does not itself market custody services to the Hong Kong public.

Individual licensing (or accreditation as a relevant individual) will be required for senior management overseeing custody. It also covers anyone with direct access to private keys or authority to approve transfers, multi-signature participants, and those with access to key generation/recovery systems. Purely clerical staff are excluded.

A licensed VA custodian's baseline financial resources will be paid-up share capital of at least HK$10 million and liquid capital of at least HK$3 million. This matches the Type 13 (depositary services) standard, though banks instead rely on their existing HKMA capital rules.
No deeming/grandfathering arrangement will apply. The regime takes full effect on the commencement date, though an expedited approval track is available for entities already assessed by SFC or HKMA.
HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuers custodying only the stablecoins they themselves issue for their own clients are exempt from needing a separate VA custodian licence.

SFC intends to use the VATP Guidelines' Chapter X custody standards (including the existing 98/2 cold/hot storage benchmark referenced by respondents) as the baseline for the new custodian regulatory requirements.
Licensed VA custodians will be permitted to offer staking services, subject to safeguards similar to those already required of VATPs offering staking.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This defines exactly which of the bank's VA-custody-adjacent functions will need a licence (key-holding entities) versus which will not (trustees, delegating fund managers). Sets the individual-licensing net compliance must apply to staff with real key or signing access.

quote.text: same activity, same risks, same regulations

reading_guide: Read paras 1-35 (Scope) closely for the private-key test and exemptions, and paras 15-28 on individual licensing; skim paras 36-64 on allowed activities, fees and appeals. Skip the annex of respondents.
flags: Group entities providing only technical/operational support are not separately licensed, but individual staff at those group entities who actually hold or sign with private keys must still be accredited to the licensed entity — a distinction easy to miss when mapping group operating models.

obligations: Identify every entity/system in the group that can independently move client VAs via private keys and licence each one as a VA custodian once the regime commences (paras 6-9, p.4-5).
Identify and individually licence/accredit staff (and group-entity personnel) with real key access or transfer/signing authority, excluding clerical roles (paras 24-27, p.9-10).
Meet the HK$10m paid-up / HK$3m liquid capital baseline for any licensed custody entity, unless it is a bank relying on existing HKMA capital rules (para 42, p.14).
controls_and_monitoring: Expect a cold/hot storage standard modelled on the existing VATP 98/2 benchmark, plus expected requirements on key management, audits and business continuity once finalised (paras 43-44, p.14-15).
notifications_reporting: Engage SFC/HKMA pre-application early to access the expedited licensing track (para 50, p.16).
counterparty_due_diligence: For any third-party VA custodian used, confirm it is (or will be) SFC-licensed and confirm which group entity actually holds the private keys, since delegation to a sub-custodian does not itself require a separate licence at the delegating layer (paras 6-9, p.4-5).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board/risk committee should hear that custody licensing attaches to whoever holds the keys — including named individuals — so the bank's group custody operating model and staff access list need mapping against this test before the regime commences.

title: FSTB and SFC conclude consultations on virtual asset dealer and custodian regimes, further consult on two new regimes
summary: This press release announces that the FSTB and SFC have finished reviewing the mid-2025 VA dealing and VA custodian consultations and will move ahead with both licensing regimes. Citing broad market support (over 190 responses) under the ASPIRe roadmap's 'Access' pillar. VA dealers will be regulated in a way that tracks Type 1 (securities dealing). VA custodians will be regulated around how they keep client VAs' private keys safe within Hong Kong. At the same time, a further consultation was launched on new VA advisory and VA management service provider regimes, with comments due 23 January 2026. A bill covering all these regimes is targeted for introduction to LegCo in 2026.

key_points.point: FSTB and SFC will proceed with legislative proposals for VA dealer and VA custodian regimes following broad market support.
The VA dealer regime will closely track the Type 1 (dealing in securities) regulated activity set out in the SFO, with comparable exemptions being considered.
The VA custodian regime will centre on the risks of keeping client VAs' private keys secure within Hong Kong.
Interested parties are encouraged to initiate pre-application discussions with the SFC to prepare for the proposed regimes.
Further consultation launched the same day on new VA advisory and VA management service provider regimes, modelled on comparable securities-market regulation.
Over 190 responses were received across the two original consultations (VA dealer and VA custodian).
Comments on the VA advisor and manager regimes further consultation are due to FSTB or SFC by 23 January 2026.
FSTB and SFC intend to finalise legislative proposals under the AMLO (Cap. 615) and introduce a bill into LegCo in 2026.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This confirms Hong Kong's VA regulatory perimeter is expanding into dealing, custody, advisory and management as separately licensable activities under one forthcoming bill. A compliance head should map which of the bank's activities will need which licence and start SFC pre-application discussions early.

quote.text: same business, same risks, same rules

reading_guide: Short press release; read in full (about 1 page); notes at the end give background context only.

notifications_reporting: Begin pre-application discussions with the SFC now to prepare for the VA dealer and VA custodian regimes ahead of the 2026 bill (para 4)
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should be told a single 2026 AMLO bill will cover VA dealer, custodian, advisory and management regimes, and pre-application engagement is encouraged now (Note 3).

title: SFC reprimands and fines Saxo Capital Markets HK Limited $4 million for regulatory breaches over distribution of virtual asset-related products
summary: The SFC reprimanded Saxo Capital Markets HK Limited (SCMHK) and imposed a HK$4 million fine. The fine was for selling 32 unauthorised virtual-asset (VA) funds and VA-related products to retail and professional clients through its online trading platform. This ran over roughly four years, from late 2018 to late 2022, in breach of two SFC circulars that limit such products to professional investors.

key_points.point: SCMHK was fined HK$4 million and reprimanded for selling VA products to retail and professional investor (PI) clients, breaching 2018 and 2022 circulars that limit such products to professional investors.

During the relevant period (1 November 2018 to 25 November 2022), SCMHK executed 1,446 trades across 32 VA products, including 21 exchange-traded derivatives. These trades were on behalf of six individual PIs plus 130 retail clients.
SCMHK never checked whether clients understood VA products or gave enough VA-specific information and warnings before executing trades, breaching circular guidance.

SCMHK had no dedicated due-diligence process for VA products and instead relied on a flawed group-wide check that missed all 32 products as VA-related. All 32 products were sold to clients regardless of PI status.
The SFC found SCMHK failed to check whether complex VA products suited each client and failed to give enough risk and feature information plus warnings on its online platform.
For 87 clients who traded exchange-traded derivative VA products, SCMHK failed to properly check and record their derivatives knowledge.
The breaches involved two instruments: the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the SFC, and the Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms.

Factors reducing the penalty: SCMHK reported itself, voluntarily paid clients back, stopped regulated activities from 28 February 2025, cooperated, and had a clean disciplinary history. The misconduct lasting over four years counted against it.

numbers_and_dates.value: 32 products; 1,446 transactions; 6 individual PIs + 130 retail clients

numbers_and_dates.item: Exchange-traded derivative VA Products / affected clients

Knowledge tests or warnings, gives a useful benchmark for the bank's own online product-identification and suitability controls. Shows the value of self-reporting.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Brief the board/risk committee on this HK$4 million fine as an example of enforcement risk from weak VA-product identification and suitability controls on an online trading platform, and note how self-reporting and fixing problems helped reduce the penalty.

title: Circular to Licensed Corporations, SFC-licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers and Associated Entities - Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism Transition to the new suspicious transaction reporting platform
supersedes_or_amends: STREAMS suspicious transaction reporting platform
summary: This SFC circular tells licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual-asset service providers and their associated entities about a platform switch. The Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) is switching from the STREAMS platform to the new STREAMS 2 platform for filing suspicious transaction reports (STRs), effective 2 February 2026. It sets out the three allowed submission methods: XML file, uploading a set PDF form, or a web form. It also covers account sign-up steps, and a blackout window from midnight on 28 January 2026 to 9am on 2 February 2026. During that window, any urgent STR must go straight to the JFIU by email, phone or fax.

key_points.point: From 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 becomes the only way to file STRs, replacing the old STREAMS platform.
Licensed firms must file STRs on STREAMS 2 using one of three formats. These are XML format (needs a Hongkong Post e-Cert), a preset PDF form upload (also needs an e-Cert), or the web-based STR form.
Licensed firms should sign up for STREAMS 2 accounts by sending a registration form to the JFIU by email, so they can file promptly.
STREAMS stops taking submissions from midnight on 28 January 2026, and STREAMS 2 starts taking them again at 9am on 2 February 2026. This gap is the blackout window.
During the blackout window, urgent STRs must go straight to the JFIU by email, phone (2866 3366) or fax (2529 4013).
All STRs filed earlier through STREAMS will move over to STREAMS 2, including any consent status attached to them.
Firms planning to file via XML must follow the JFIU's XML format and arrange a test with the JFIU as soon as possible.
Any STR sent to the JFIU by a channel other than STREAMS 2 after the switch must be re-filed through STREAMS 2.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This is a firm operational deadline for the bank's SFC-licensed corporation or trading-platform subsidiary, not for the bank itself as an Authorized Institution (AI). Files STRs under a separate HKMA AML/CFT channel. The Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) should confirm which entity's filings this switch affects before 2 February 2026.

quote.text: STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs

reading_guide: Read in full; it is a short two-page operational circular with a clear timeline.

obligations: If the bank runs an SFC-licensed corporation or trading platform that files STRs, sign up for STREAMS 2 accounts and, if filing by XML, finish JFIU testing before 2 February 2026 (p.1; para (d), p.2).
notifications_reporting: Send urgent STRs straight to the JFIU by email, phone or fax during the blackout window (midnight 28 Jan 2026 to 9am 2 Feb 2026) rather than through STREAMS (para (a)-(b), p.2).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: The board and MLRO should note this circular targets the bank's SFC-licensed corporation or trading-platform entity specifically; the bank's own STR duties as an AI under the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline run through a separate channel and should be checked independently.

title: SFC and UAE's Capital Market Authority sign milestone MoU to strengthen cross-border digital asset collaboration
summary: The SFC and the UAE's Capital Market Authority (CMA) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to deepen cross-border regulatory teamwork on digital-asset matters. The SFC's first agreement with an overseas regulator focused specifically on supervising regulated digital-asset firms. The MoU sets up a framework for the two regulators to consult each other and share information when overseeing cross-border digital-asset entities, under the SFC's ASPIRe roadmap. It follows and expands on a Mutual Recognition of Funds MoU the two regulators signed in September 2025, and was announced alongside an industry event on UAE fund distribution.

key_points.point: This is the SFC's first agreement with a foreign regulator built specifically for joint supervision of regulated digital-asset entities.
The MoU sets up a channel for the two regulators to consult each other and exchange information to help supervise digital-asset firms operating across both markets.
CMA CEO H.E. Waleed Saeed Al Awadhi and SFC CEO Ms Julia Leung signed the agreement, with SFC Chairman Dr Kelvin Wong present.
This digital-asset MoU builds on an earlier fund-recognition agreement the two regulators signed in September 2025. It lets each side's public funds be offered in the other's market.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: Shows Hong Kong and the UAE stepping up cooperation on supervising digital-asset businesses -- worth noting for a bank with UAE ties or plans for cross-border digital-asset activity.

quote.text: This MoU strengthens supervisory cooperation between the CMA and the SFC on regulated digital

reading_guide: Read in full; short press release with quotes; notes provide background only.

title: HKMA unveils Fintech Promotion Blueprint: From adoption to advancement
summary: The HKMA published its Fintech Promotion Blueprint under the 'Fintech 2030' strategy. It focuses on more sophisticated applications of AI and distributed ledger technology (DLT), enabled by high-performance computing (HPC), with Data Excellence and Cyber Resilience as foundational pillars. Four flagship projects were announced: a Quantum Preparedness Index to assess banks' post-quantum cryptography readiness, and a New Risk Data Strategy to strengthen bank data governance and infrastructure. Two more were also announced: a Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline for fintech solution providers to streamline bank due-diligence, and Competency Development Support for fintech users. The Blueprint also introduces FiNETech events, innovation competitions, a revamped Fintech Connect matching platform, and workshops, responding to challenges identified in the HKMA's Tech Maturity Stock-take.

key_points.point: The Blueprint sits under 'Fintech 2030' and is structured around three tactical dimensions: Ecosystem Collaboration, Technological Advancement, and Talent and Outreach, with Data Excellence and Cyber Resilience as foundational pillars.

The HKMA plans to build a Quantum Preparedness Index. This gauges how ready the banking sector is for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), giving both a snapshot of where things stand now and a measurable target over several years.
A New Risk Data Strategy will enhance banks' data management capabilities and data governance frameworks to support advanced AI/DLT analytics and expand the HKMA's Granular Data Reporting initiative.

A new industry-led Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline will be established with industry experts for fintech solution providers using AI/DLT, to improve due-diligence efficiency for banks onboarding fintech partners.
Competency development support will provide practical guidance to enhance skills of general fintech users, with a focus on 'human-machine interaction' capability.

The Blueprint responds to challenges identified in the HKMA's Tech Maturity Stock-take via FiNETech events, responsible innovation competitions, a revamped Fintech Connect matching platform, and practical workshops.

numbers_and_dates.value: Fintech Adoption: Progress and Future Directions, HKMA (2025)

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This is not yet binding, but a compliance head should still track the Quantum Preparedness Index and the Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline. Both are likely future supervisory expectations relevant to any DLT-enabled digital-asset product's technology and vendor risk management.

title: SFC convenes third Digital Asset Consultative Panel meeting
summary: The SFC held the third meeting of its Digital Asset Consultative Panel (DACP). A forum where the SFC's licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) come together to discuss upcoming regulatory developments. Participants discussed initiatives to strengthen the digital asset ecosystem, including steps to boost liquidity on licensed VATPs and widen the range of products and services. The DACP is chaired by Dr Eric Yip, the SFC's Executive Director of Intermediaries, and works under Pillar Re (Relationships) of the ASPIRe roadmap.

key_points.point: The SFC held the third DACP meeting with SFC-licensed VATPs to discuss coming digital asset regulatory developments.
Topics discussed included regulatory steps to boost liquidity on licensed VATPs and to widen product and service offerings.
The DACP works in line with Pillar Re (Relationships) of the SFC's ASPIRe roadmap, supporting ongoing collaboration with licensed VATPs.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This signals the SFC's ongoing industry-engagement channel (DACP). Previewing coming liquidity and product-expansion steps for licensed VATPs — useful for anticipating future circulars, such as those on shared order books and financing.

quote.text: balancing innovation with robust investor protection

reading_guide: Short press release; read in full (under 1 page).

title: SFC launches trading initiatives to boost digital asset market vibrancy in Hong Kong
summary: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) announced three initiatives on the same day, aimed at boosting liquidity in Hong Kong's digital asset market under the ASPIRe roadmap. First, virtual asset (VA) brokers may offer financing to securities margin clients, under a circular covering VA financing and shared order book access. Second, for the first time, the SFC issued a high-level framework letting licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) build leveraged perpetual contracts. This is limited to professional investors, and covers product design, disclosure and operating controls. Third, affiliates of licensed VATPs may now act as market makers on those platforms, subject to safeguards against conflicts of interest, under a separate circular on affiliated market makers.

key_points.point: VA brokers can now offer financing to their securities margin clients, as long as collateral is sufficient and strong investor protections are in place. This lets creditworthy margin clients trade more VA.

For the first time, the SFC issued a high-level framework for licensed VATPs to build leveraged perpetual contracts. These are offered only to professional investors, with clear product design, disclosure and strong operating controls.
Affiliates of licensed VATPs may now act as market makers on those same platforms, as long as strong safeguards limit conflicts of interest.
These three initiatives carry out the SFC's ASPIRe roadmap goal of widening the range of products and services and improving liquidity.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This widens what SFC-licensed VA brokers and VATPs may offer, such as margin financing, leveraged perpetual contracts, and affiliated market makers. The bank is not directly bound, but compliance should weigh the new leverage and conflict-of-interest risks when reviewing any VATP or VA broker counterparty.

quote.text: unswerving commitment to developing Hong Kong's digital asset market in a sustainable and collaborative manner

reading_guide: Short press release; read in full, then cross-reference the same-day circulars 26EC5 (VA financing/shared order book) and 26EC6 (affiliated market makers) for detail. The perpetual contracts framework referenced in Note 3 is a separate document not included in this batch.
flags: References 'A high-level framework for virtual asset perpetual contracts offering by virtual asset trading platforms', a new same-day SFC framework document not itself included in this document set - first-time SFC guidance permitting VATP-offered leveraged/perpetual VA contracts, restricted to professional investors, worth sourcing separately.

counterparty_due_diligence: If a VATP counterparty offers leveraged products such as perpetual contracts, check that it only serves professional investors under the SFC's high-level framework, with clear product design, disclosures, and operating controls, before referring clients or using the products.

Note that a VATP's affiliates may now act as market makers on that VATP's own platform, subject to conflict-of-interest safeguards. Factor this into how the bank assesses that counterparty's conflicts.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: The board should be told that VA margin financing and leveraged perpetual contracts are now allowed for licensed brokers and VATPs. This wider product set raises counterparty and market-structure risk wherever the bank's clients use these venues.

title: A high-level framework for virtual asset perpetual contracts offering by virtual asset trading platforms
summary: The SFC set out, at a high level, the conditions under which its licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) may offer perpetual contracts (Perps) — leveraged. No-expiry derivatives whose price tracks a reference virtual asset via periodic funding payments. Perps may only be offered to professional investors and only over spot assets already tradable by retail clients on the platform, or an IOSCO-compliant index of such assets. The framework prescribes margining, valuation, liquidation and disclosure standards, and requires margin to be posted in fiat, HKMA-regulated stablecoins or tokenised deposits only, with no credit extended for margin. Platform operators are invited to bring proposed Perp structures to the SFC for discussion before launch.

key_points.point: Perpetual contracts may only be offered to professional investors, not retail clients, and only after the platform assesses each client's derivatives knowledge under the Code of Conduct.
A Perp's reference asset must already be tradable in spot form by retail clients on the same platform, or must be an index of such assets compliant with IOSCO benchmark principles.
Margin collateral is restricted to fiat currency, or to stablecoins or tokenised deposits that are HKMA-regulated; platforms may not extend credit for margin.
key_points.locator: section 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management'

key_points.point: Platforms must maintain a pre-defined loss-allocation hierarchy (order-book liquidation, backstop liquidity, reserve/insurance fund, auto-deleveraging, other last resort) and disclose the triggers for each to clients.
key_points.locator: section 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management'

key_points.point: Funding-rate payments between long and short position holders must occur at least once every 24 hours, following methodologies that are transparent, verifiable, and calculated in real time.

Pricing references (mark price, index) must draw on multiple independent sources to reduce single-entity manipulation risk, with disclosed compilation methodology and contingency/failover arrangements.

If the insurance fund is depleted or unavailable, platforms must promptly notify all open-position clients and warn that auto-deleveraging may follow. A post-event report is required within 24 hours of any auto-deleveraging.
key_points.locator: section 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management'

key_points.point: Platforms should implement real-time cross-market surveillance covering both spot and Perp trading to catch manipulation patterns specific to Perps.
The SFC frames this as an initial, high-level framework that may be refined, and operators are encouraged to bring proposed Perp structures to the SFC for discussion before offering them.

numbers_and_dates.locator: section 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management'

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: If the bank's clients trade Perps via an SFC-licensed VATP, compliance should confirm the platform is following this framework. This matters especially for the professional-investor gate and the HKMA-regulated-collateral rule, before treating any related exposure as within the regulated perimeter for due-diligence purposes.
reading_guide: Read the whole document; it is short (one page of continuous text) with no page or paragraph numbering, organised by section headings from 'Scope of application' through 'Disclosure requirements'.
flags: Document uses no paragraph numbers; locators are by section heading only, as instructed for documents lacking numbering.

controls_and_monitoring: If the bank's clients access Perps through a VATP, compliance can use this framework as a due-diligence checklist: professional-investor gating, permitted margin collateral types, and disclosure of loss-allocation triggers (whole document).
counterparty_due_diligence: Check that any VATP counterparty offering Perps to bank-referred or bank clients restricts access to professional investors and accepts only fiat or HKMA-regulated stablecoins/tokenised deposits as margin (section 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; section 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management').
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should be told the SFC now permits licensed platforms to offer leveraged Perps to professional investors under a new but still-evolving high-level framework, relevant if the bank refers or services such clients.

title: Circular on licensed corporations providing virtual asset dealing services (1) to offer financing for virtual asset dealing and access to shared order book, and (2) to safeguard client virtual assets relating to withdrawals
supersedes_or_amends: Terms and Conditions for VA dealing under an omnibus account arrangement (prohibition on financial accommodation)
summary: The SFC lets VA brokers (licensed corporations dealing in VAs through omnibus accounts at licensed platforms) that already run securities margin financing lend to margin clients for VA trades. Credit must rest on the client's financial capacity and on securities and a narrow set of VA collateral: bitcoin and ether only, with a haircut of at least 60%. Brokers must assess VA-specific risks, monitor collateral in real time, apply existing margin-lending rules and not reuse VA collateral. The circular also sets conditions for agency trading on shared order books linked to overseas affiliates, including explicit opt-in for retail clients. Requires stronger controls where brokers let clients withdraw VAs. The HKMA circulated this same SFC circular to registered institutions (RIs) as an attachment to its own circular dated 27 May 2026. The HKMA circular's own covering text was not captured in the fetched source for this entry, so any bank-specific modifications (for example, to eligible collateral or capital treatment) it may make are not verified here.

key_points.point: Before this, firms were barred from giving clients credit to buy VAs; the SFC now allows it as a first step under its ASPIRe roadmap.
Financing is limited to existing securities margin clients and based on their financial capacity plus posted collateral.
Firms should not raise credit limits just because VA financing is available, and should weigh VA-specific risks when counting VAs toward net worth.
VA collateral is limited to bitcoin and ether with a haircut of at least 60%, which the SFC may revise on notice.
Firms relying on VA collateral must document methods in the margin policy and monitor collateral volatility in real time.
Firms should value collateral using prices on the platform where the client's orders execute, with a contingency plan for platform outages.
Existing margin rules extend to VA financing; VA collateral cannot be repledged or reused except on client default.
Where the loan exceeds collateral value or margin calls go unpaid, stop further advances and VA purchases and review limits.
Until capital rules are revised, VA collateral gets a 100% haircut under the Financial Resources Rules.
Agency trading on a shared order book needs a prior risk assessment (conflicts, settlement, failure scenarios, reserves, client recourse) and clear disclosure.
Retail clients may access a shared order book only after the overseas risks are prominently explained and they expressly opt in.
Where clients can withdraw VAs, brokers must harden authentication and access, monitor around the clock with escalation and suspension, and work with platforms on withdrawal limits and blocking.

numbers_and_dates.item: FRR treatment of VA collateral pending consultation

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: The fetched text for this entry is the SFC circular itself. The HKMA is confirmed (via the BRDR listing) to have issued it to RIs on 27 May 2026. The HKMA cover circular's own substantive text was not fetched, so compliance should obtain and read that HKMA circular directly rather than assume it mirrors the SFC terms.

quote.text: eligible VA collateral should be limited to bitcoin and ether

reading_guide: Read paras 4-11 (financing), 16-17 (shared order book) and 19-20 (withdrawals). Para 14 on capital applies to LCs only.
flags: As an SFC circular it binds LCs directly; the HKMA is confirmed to have attached it to a 27 May 2026 circular addressed to Registered Institutions, but that HKMA circular's own body text (e.g. any changes to eligible collateral or capital treatment for banks) was not captured in the fetched source and is not verified by this entry.

obligations: For RIs (via HKMA): obtain and review the HKMA's 27 May 2026 circular directly, since its own text (including any paragraphs on shared order books or client VA withdrawals) was not captured for this entry.
controls_and_monitoring: Real-time VA collateral monitoring; documented VA risk methodology in margin policy (para 8).
Margin call and stop-advance triggers (para 11).
24/7 withdrawal monitoring, escalation and suspension; strong authentication (para 20).
counterparty_due_diligence: Before using a shared order book: assess the operators' conflicts, settlement mechanism, default management, reserve fund/insurance and client recourse (para 16).
Coordinate with the VATP on omnibus-level and new-wallet withdrawal limits and blocking (para 20(c)).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: VA margin lending is now possible but tightly bounded; board should set risk appetite, collateral limits and confirm withdrawal cyber controls before any launch, and should separately review the HKMA cover circular text applicable to the bank.

title: Circular on licensed corporations providing virtual asset dealing services (1) to offer financing for virtual asset dealing and access to shared order book, and (2) to safeguard client virtual assets relating to withdrawals
supersedes_or_amends: Terms and Conditions for Licensed Corporations or Registered Institutions Providing Virtual Asset Dealing Services under an Omnibus Account Arrangement
summary: This SFC circular relaxes the prior prohibition on financial accommodation for VA dealing. It lets VA brokers (licensed corporations providing VA dealing services under an omnibus account arrangement) that already conduct securities margin financing extend VA financing to margin clients, subject to strict conditions. Eligible VA collateral is limited to bitcoin and ether with a haircut of 60% or more. The circular also extends existing Securities Margin Financing Guidelines controls and sets specific credit-risk factors to assess. It also lets VA brokers act as agent on a Shared Order Book that matches orders across affiliated VATPs. This is subject to risk assessment and, for retail clients, explicit risk disclosure and opt-in. Finally, it sets expected controls for VA brokers offering client VA withdrawal functionality, given the added cyber/operational risk of fraudulent withdrawal instructions.

key_points.point: VA brokers engaging in securities margin financing may now extend VA financing to margin clients, based on financial capability plus securities and/or VA collateral. This relaxes the prior blanket prohibition on financial accommodation for VA dealing.

Eligible VA clients for financing are limited to the broker's existing securities margin financing clients. Brokers must not increase a client's credit limit solely because VA financing becomes available.
If VA collateral is used as credit risk mitigation, it must be limited to bitcoin and ether only, with a prudent haircut of 60% or more applied to its market value.
Until a planned consultation revises capital requirements, VA collateral must be treated with a full 100% haircut, per the Securities and Futures (Financial Resources) Rules.
VA brokers must not repledge, reuse or create encumbrance over VA collateral other than to enforce it upon client default.

VA brokers may conduct agency trading on a Shared Order Book (cross-platform order matching among affiliate VATPs). Before doing so, they must assess conflicts of interest, the settlement mechanism, failed-settlement or default processes, risk mitigation measures, and client protection or recourse.

Retail clients may only access the Shared Order Book if the broker has explained the additional overseas-jurisdiction risks (including potentially lower client protection) and the client has expressly elected to participate.

VA brokers offering client VA withdrawal functionality must implement robust authentication and access controls, plus continuous monitoring with incident escalation. They must also collaborate with VATP operators on withdrawal limits and suspicious-withdrawal detection, given the risk of fraudulent withdrawal instructions from a compromised broker system.

numbers_and_dates.item: VA collateral haircut (financing, once capital rules revised)
VA collateral haircut (interim, before capital rules revised)

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This binds the bank's SFC-licensed VA-dealing subsidiary directly. It sets credit-risk, collateral-eligibility and withdrawal-security controls the compliance head must build into the bank's VA brokerage product design before any VA-collateralised margin lending goes live.

quote.text: a prudent haircut of 60% or more

reading_guide: Read paras 1-14 (VA financing) and paras 18-20 (withdrawal safeguards) closely. Paras 15-17 (Shared Order Book) are secondary if the bank's VA broker does not use shared order books.
flags: Corrects an assumption that SFC-licensed VA dealing remains purely cash/spot: this circular formally opens the door to VA-collateralised margin lending, though currently neutralised by a 100% interim haircut pending a capital requirements consultation.
VA collateral eligibility is narrowly restricted to bitcoin and ether only, not the broader VA universe a firm may trade.

obligations: If the bank's SFC-licensed VA broker extends VA financing, limit eligible VA collateral to bitcoin and ether with a haircut of 60% or more (currently 100% under the interim capital rule) and only to existing securities margin financing clients (paras 5-7, 14, p.1-3).
Do not repledge, reuse, or encumber VA collateral except to enforce it on client default (para 10(c), p.3).
controls_and_monitoring: If offering client VA withdrawal functionality, implement robust authentication/access controls, continuous monitoring with incident escalation, and coordinate with VATP operators on withdrawal limits and suspicious-withdrawal detection (paras 19-20, p.4-5).
counterparty_due_diligence: Before enabling Shared Order Book access, assess the affiliate VATP's conflicts of interest, settlement mechanism, default process and client recourse (paras 15-16, p.3-4).
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board/credit risk committee should be told VA collateral is currently neutralised by a 100% interim haircut (para 14, p.3) pending a forthcoming capital rules consultation, before approving any VA-collateralised margin product.

title: Circular on permitting virtual asset trading platform operators to accept affiliated market makers
supersedes_or_amends: Guidelines for Virtual Asset Trading Platform Operators (paragraph 13.3, group companies proprietary trading restriction)
summary: This SFC circular permits SFC-licensed VATP operators, for the first time as a general policy rather than case-by-case, to allow an affiliated company (an affiliated market maker. AFMM) to conduct market making on their platform, in order to address subdued VATP liquidity under Pillar A (Access) of the ASPIRe roadmap. Permission is conditional on effective conflicts-of-interest controls (functional independence, information barriers, client order priority, post-trade AFMM trade identification. Disclosure of preferential treatment), binding Terms and Conditions imposed on the operator's licence (set out in an Appendix). A mandatory prior notification to the SFC accompanied by an independent professional firm's compliance report, signed off by the Manager-in-Charge of Overall Management Oversight (MIC OMO).

key_points.point: Under the current VATP Guidelines (para 13.3), a Platform Operator's group companies are generally barred from proprietary trading through the Platform Operator, except where the SFC permits it case-by-case. This circular sets a general framework to permit an AFMM to market-make.
A Platform Operator must ensure the AFMM is functionally independent, with organisational and administrative segregation from the Platform Operator's operating environment.

Platform operators must make sure client orders rank ahead of AFMM orders whenever they trade at the same price. They must also be able to flag which trades in post-trade data were executed by the AFMM.
The Platform Operator must disclose to clients the AFMM's presence and role, any preferential treatment in pre-trade transparency/order placing/execution, and associated risks.
At least one Responsible Officer or MIC must be designated to oversee conflicts of interest management regarding the AFMM.

Before allowing AFMM market making, the Platform Operator must notify the SFC in writing and submit an independent professional firm's report confirming the effectiveness of its Terms and Conditions compliance controls.

The MIC of Overall Management Oversight (MIC OMO) must sign the notification to the SFC, confirming that compliance policies are in place. They must also pledge to immediately halt AFMM market making the moment a breach affects clients significantly, in the SFC's judgement.

The AFMM must get the same technical access as other market makers get, including market data feeds, connectivity, and order types. Its orders and trades must be captured in the operator's market surveillance systems.
The Platform Operator must immediately report to the SFC any actual or potential material breach of the Terms and Conditions, or any regulatory or law enforcement action against the AFMM.
Compliance with the AFMM Terms and Conditions must be covered in the Platform Operator's annual independent professional firm review reported to the SFC.

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This binds VATPs, not the bank directly. If the bank's VATP-affiliated entity wants to market-make on its own platform, a compliance head must ensure the conflicts-of-interest. Disclosure and SFC pre-notification framework here is fully built before commencing.

quote.text: client orders should always have priority over the AFMM's orders

reading_guide: Read the main circular (paras 1-11) for the policy rationale and notification process, then the Appendix Terms and Conditions in full as they are the binding licence conditions.
flags: Marks a shift from strict case-by-case exceptions to a standing framework allowing affiliated (non-independent) market makers on VATPs - a notable departure from the general prohibition on group proprietary trading through the platform operator.

counterparty_due_diligence: If the bank's VATP affiliate wants to allow an affiliated market maker, confirm functional independence, client-order priority and disclosure controls are in place, and that a compliance report was filed with the SFC before commencing (paras 7, 9-10)
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: If a bank-group VATP intends to use an affiliated market maker, board should be told this requires prior written SFC notification, an independent report, and an MIC OMO declaration with an undertaking to suspend on breach (paras 9-10).

title: The 2026-27 Budget — Speech by the Financial Secretary
summary: In the digital-asset section of the 2026-27 Budget Speech, the Financial Secretary confirmed plans to introduce a bill in 2026 licensing digital asset dealing and custodian service providers. Noted the first batch of stablecoin issuer licences would be issued the following month. The SFC will look to widen liquidity and product access for professional investors and set up an accelerator for market innovation. Separately, an Inland Revenue amendment bill will implement the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and the amended Common Reporting Standard within two years. The HKMA's CMU OmniClear will launch a digital asset platform in 2026 to support digital bond issuance and settlement, alongside continued rollout of Project Ensemble's tokenised-deposit pilot (EnsembleTX).

key_points.point: A bill to establish licensing regimes for digital asset dealing and custodian service providers will be introduced in 2026.
The first batch of stablecoin issuer licences (under the existing licensing regime for fiat-referenced stablecoin issuers) was due to be issued the month after the speech.

The SFC intends to broaden digital-asset market liquidity and product/service offerings for professional investors, subject to sufficient investor protection, and will set up an accelerator to speed up market innovation.
Government will issue guidelines clarifying that debenture-holder registers may be kept as a distributed ledger, to support tokenisation of bond issuance and trading.

The Government plans to bring a bill amending the Inland Revenue Ordinance to adopt the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and the OECD's updated Common Reporting Standard. This is planned sometime in the year's first six months, with the two-year rollout starting after that.

Project Ensemble's pilot phase, EnsembleTX (launched the previous November), lets industry participants transact in tokenised deposits and digital assets in a controlled pilot environment. The HKMA will keep upgrading it toward 24/7 settlement and cross-market interoperability standards.

CMU OmniClear will launch a digital asset platform in 2026 to support issuance and settlement of digital bonds. There are plans to extend it to other digital assets and link with regional tokenisation platforms.

The Government will widen family-office tax concessions to treat digital assets, along with precious metals and specified commodities, as qualifying investments. This will be done through a bill due in the year's first six months, aiming to take effect from the 2025/26 year of assessment.

The Government issued a third batch of tokenised government bonds (HK$10 billion) in Q4 of the prior year, settled with an option for tokenised central bank money. It will continue regular tokenised bond issuance, with HKMA encouraging further digital bond issuance via the Digital Bond Grant Scheme.

numbers_and_dates.item: third batch tokenised government bond issuance size

numbers_and_dates.value: within the coming two years, IRO amendment bill in H1 of the Budget year

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: The speech confirms government-level timelines the bank should track against its own build plans. The dealing/custodian licensing bill, first stablecoin-issuer licences, and the CARF tax-reporting bill all land or advance in 2026. CMU OmniClear's new digital asset platform also signals where institutional tokenised-bond settlement infrastructure is heading.
reading_guide: Skip most of the 180+ page speech. Go straight to paras 96-115 (pp.37-42), the 'Develop Fintech and Financial Infrastructure' and adjacent bond-market/asset-management subsections, which contain every digital-asset-relevant passage.
flags: This is a political speech, not a legal instrument; all 'will'/'plan to' statements are policy intentions with no binding force until implemented through the referenced bills or regulatory issuances.

bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Board should note the government's 2026 policy calendar for digital assets — dealing/custodian licensing bill, first stablecoin licences, CARF tax reporting bill, and CMU OmniClear's digital asset platform — as context for the bank's own digital-asset roadmap and budget planning.

The initiative also plans to connect with the HKMA's existing Commercial Data Interchange and CargoX projects to support trade-finance data facilitation.

title: Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Shanghai Data Bureau, and National Technology Innovation Center for Blockchain sign MoU to strengthen Shanghai-Hong Kong cooperation in digitised cargo trade and finance

They will also study how trade finance could move faster using cargo and trade data. Linking to the Commercial Data Interchange (CDI) on one side and Cargo X on the other.

The three sides will jointly research digital-technology uses in cargo trade and finance, and weigh up building a cross-border platform.

title: Digital Asset Consultative Panel

title: Strategic Review of Business Models amid Digital Transformation
summary: This HKMA circular (reference B1/15C, dated 9 March 2026, signed by Deputy Chief Executive Arthur Yuen) tells banks to actively rethink their long-term business models. This is in light of digitalisation, distributed ledger technology (DLT), agentic artificial intelligence (AI), and cloud or high-performance computing. It refers to the HKMA's Fintech Promotion Blueprint under 'Fintech 2030'. It asks each bank's board to oversee and approve a formal strategic business plan covering these changes, within six months of the circular. A bank may optionally use the Supervisory Incubator for DLT to test new business models. It confirms banks must still discuss any new digital-asset activity with the HKMA before launching it.

key_points.point: Digitalisation, especially the spread of distributed ledger technology (DLT), is reshaping customer expectations and the financial landscape. The HKMA says agentic AI, cloud computing and high-performance computing are speeding up this shift.

The HKMA expects each Authorized Institution's Board of Directors to oversee and approve, within six months of the circular's date, a formal strategic business plan covering these technology shifts. This spans products, revenue models, customer engagement, risk management and operations where relevant.
As part of that plan, a bank may choose to run small, real-world trials through the HKMA's Supervisory Incubator for DLT to test new business models.
Some Authorized Institutions will be asked to submit their strategic business plans through the HKMA's Survey Tool.
As is already the practice, banks entering new digital-asset activities are still expected to talk through their plans with the HKMA before launching.

numbers_and_dates.item: deadline for board to endorse a strategic business plan
numbers_and_dates.value: within six months from the date of the circular (i.e. by approximately 9 September 2026)

why_it_matters_for_bank_HoDA: This creates a specific, dated board-level task — a strategic plan covering DLT and digital transformation. Due within six months — and restates the standing rule that any new digital-asset activity must be discussed with the HKMA first. Compliance needs to track and calendar both.

quote.text: AIs intending to expand into new digital asset-related activities are expected to discuss

reading_guide: Read the full two-page letter; it is short and entirely about the strategic business-plan expectation and DLT-related digital transformation.
flags: This attachment's own metadata record lists its parent as a different document id (28c1f4e0090b) and describes it as 'Opening Remarks at Tokenisation: Banking the Future', but the actual PDF text is unambiguously this 9 March 2026 circular addressed to All Authorized Institutions and signed by Arthur Yuen — a metadata/attachment-id mismatch in the corpus, not a content error; entry is based on the actual text.

This circular does not itself use the words 'cryptoasset', 'virtual asset', 'stablecoin' or 'tokenis-'; its only crypto-adjacent content is the two references to DLT as a driver of digital transformation, plus the pointer to the Supervisory Incubator for DLT and the standing digital-asset pre-launch consultation expectation.

obligations: Make sure the Board of Directors oversees and approves a formal strategic business plan covering digital transformation, including DLT, within six months of 9 March 2026.
Keep discussing any planned new digital-asset activity with the HKMA before it launches.
notifications_reporting: Some Authorized Institutions will be asked to submit their strategic business plan through the HKMA's Survey Tool. No fixed deadline is set for this beyond the six-month board-approval window.
bank_compliance_angle.board_escalation: Schedule the board to review and approve the strategic business plan well ahead of the roughly 9 September 2026 deadline, and remind them that any new digital-asset business line still needs prior discussion with the HKMA.
